content.content:
query_dedicated_port
are physical ports used by the Steam game server api to fill sessions browser. For LAN games query_dedicated_port has be in range of <27015,27020>.
For port forwarding both TPP/IP and UPD rules are required.
Virtual ports do not need forwarding.
Server logon token
By default, whenever a dedicated server is launched it is using an anonymous account. For such an account non-persistent server id is generated (used for direct search). To avoid this you can acquire a logon token on
https://steamcommunity.com/dev/managegameservers
(game ownership is required). This token has to be placed into server_config.
Use the game appID to generate token, not the server appID!
Example:
server_logon_token: 6544F7E034119F113526E96474F
Session moderators
As the dedicated server does not have any form or user interface, it is not possible to promote any player to a moderator while the session is running. You can register moderators in server_config using their steam_id to automatically promote them once they join the session.
Example for two moderators:
moderator_list: 2
moderator_list[0]: 123456789
moderator_list[1]: 234567891
where 123456789 is the moderator's Steam id
Quality of life
Any player who is a moderator can now change the game time or disable rain. This can be done via chat message box by sending a message containing an admin command.
Available admin commands are
/set_time <HH:MM>
/set_rain_factor <value from 0 to 1>
/help
How to close server
Press Ctrl + C.
Troubleshooting
In server home folder server.log.txt and server.crash.txt (when server crashes) files can be found to help solve any issue with a dedicated server.
Known issues
When server is closed with message:
[MP] Steam disconnected
[MP] Session closure requested (reason - 33).
[MP] Session closing
It is caused by Steam losing connection. This can happen when internet connection is lost, or when the computer switches to sleep mode.
Will be fixed in next patch.

lobby_name: "Euro Truck Simulator 2 server"            // Session name, limited to 63 characters.
description: ""                                        // Session description, limited to 63 characters.
welcome_message: ""                                    // Session welcome message, limited to 127 characters.
password: ""                                           // Session password, limited to 63 characters.

max_vehicles_total: 100

server_logon_token: 6544F7E034119F113526E96474F        // Token for game server login (persistent account).
player_damage: true                                    // Flag if player can receive damage from other players.
traffic: true                                          // Flag if traffic is enabled.
hide_in_company: false                                 // Flag if remote player are hidden in company area.

This confirms it: the official documentation states server_packages.sii and .dat are absolutely required for a dedicated server to start, unconditionally, and they must be generated from the customer's own game client using the export_server_packages console command.

I'm also noting the port configuration details — virtual vs dedicated ports, default connection/query ports 27015/27016, and how server_config.sii maps to the Docker image's environment variables I found earlier from the LsHallo/ets2-dedicated-convoy-server image, which fits the platform's pattern of using community Docker images similar to Arma/CS16.

Now I'm confirming the App IDs: 1948160 for ETS2 and 2239530 for ATS's dedicated server, per SCS's own wiki. It looks like there are actually two separate published images — `lshallo/ets2-convoy-server` and `lshallo/ats-convoy-server` — each using its own matching environment variable prefix (ETS_ vs ATS_) rather than one generic image switching by APP_ID, which reconciles the conflicting README variable names I saw.

I want to check whether this popular community image (forked several times, also mirrored on ghcr.io) is truly the canonical one the platform should reference, or if something more official exists, following the same verification rigor I used for the Arma and CS16 setups.

I should still confirm the exact env var names by reviewing the docker-compose.yml or Dockerfile directly, and verify which version tags are available on Docker Hub so I can pin a specific one rather than defaulting to "latest." I also need to check whether this image supports mounting a pre-supplied server package.

Good news from the docker-compose file: it maps save data to a path like `/home/steam/.local/share/Euro Truck Simulator 2` (or the American Truck Simulator equivalent), which is exactly where server_config.sii, server_packages.sii, and server_packages.dat live. That means someone can drop exported server package files into that mounted volume and the container will use them on startup -- which directly answers whether the platform needs a genuinely new upload mechanism.

Given this, if the platform's existing file-manager/SFTP access already exposes this same per-instance data directory -- consistent with how other Docker-based game workers like Arma or CS16 handle custom content -- then customers could simply SFTP those two files in themselves, matching the existing pattern. That strongly suggests the existing infrastructure is sufficient, provided file-manager access to that persistent volume exists before the first server start.

Actually, on reflection, the container itself can start and the file can be added after an initial failed launch attempt, since the dedicated server just needs the file present before a successful restart -- so it doesn't strictly require pre-populating the volume before any container start, just before the server process itself needs to succeed.

But this raises the real crux: does the provisioning flow's health check wait for the game process to actually be up and serving before marking the server "ready" and exposing SFTP credentials to the customer? If ETS2/ATS crashes immediately without server_packages, that health check would never pass, and the customer could get stuck in a restart loop without ever seeing their SFTP access.

I need the investigation agent's findings on worker/index.ts before deciding between two paths: either the existing SFTP access is already sufficient and just needs clearer instructions pointing to the right upload directory, or the platform needs a pre-boot upload mechanism so files land in the persistent volume before the container even starts, sidestepping the crash-loop problem entirely.

Beyond that, I still want to confirm the exact Docker image tag on Docker Hub, check how other games in the platform pin versions in their Dockerfile/compose conventions, and verify American Truck Simulator's Steam app ID and port defaults match what I'd expect.

---
# You can freely choose which server to run. They don't depend on one another.
# This file gives an example config for both games.

services:
  ets2-server:
    image: lshallo/ets2-convoy-server
    # image: ghcr.io/lshallo/ets2-convoy-server # GitHub container registry
    container_name: ets2-server
    restart: unless-stopped
    tty: true
    network_mode: host # important to make game appear in server list
    # if you want to join via direct join token (displayed in logs on startup) you can use port mapping
    # the game will not appear in server list because the server can't determine the external IP
    #ports:
    #  - "27015:27015"
    #  - "27016:27016"
    #  - "27015:27015/udp"
    #  - "27016:27016/udp"
    # volumes:
    # Server files. (executable, libraries)
    # Only mount if you know what you are doing. Can lead to permissions issues.
    #  - "/opt/ets2-server/game-data:/app"
    # Only needed when using custom server_packages.sii and server_packages.dat.
    # Also keeps banlist. If you want to persist the banlist mount this folder.
    #  - "/opt/ets2-server/save-data:/home/steam/.local/share/Euro Truck Simulator 2"
    environment:
      - "ETS_SERVER_UPDATE_ON_START=true"
      - "ETS_SERVER_NAME=My Server"
      - "ETS_SERVER_DESCRIPTION=My server description"
      - "ETS_SERVER_WELCOME_MESSAGE=Welcome to my server!"
      - "ETS_SERVER_PASSWORD=abc123"
      - "ETS_SERVER_MAX_PLAYERS=8"
      - "ETS_SERVER_PORT=27015"
      - "ETS_SERVER_QUERY_PORT=27016"
      # more variables...

  ats-server:
    image: lshallo/ats-convoy-server
    # image: ghcr.io/lshallo/ats-convoy-server # GitHub container registry
    container_name: ats-server
    restart: unless-stopped
    tty: true
    network_mode: host # important to make game appear in server list
    # if you want to join via direct join token (displayed in logs on startup) you can use port mapping
    # the game will not appear in server list because the server can't determine the external IP
    #ports:
    #  - "27015:27015"
    #  - "27016:27016"
    #  - "27015:27015/udp"
    #  - "27016:27016/udp"
    # volumes:
    #  - "/opt/ats-server/game-data:/app" # server files
    #  - "/opt/ats-server/save-data:/home/steam/.local/share/American Truck Simulator" # Only needed when using custom server_packages.sii and server_packages.dat
    environment:
      - "ATS_SERVER_UPDATE_ON_START=true"
      - "ATS_SERVER_NAME=My Server"
      - "ATS_SERVER_DESCRIPTION=My server description"
      - "ATS_SERVER_WELCOME_MESSAGE=Welcome to my server!"
      - "ATS_SERVER_PASSWORD=abc123"
      - "ATS_SERVER_MAX_PLAYERS=8"
      - "ATS_SERVER_PORT=27015"
      - "ATS_SERVER_QUERY_PORT=27016"
      # more variables...
---DOCKERFILE---
FROM cm2network/steamcmd:steam

ARG APP_ID=1948160
ARG SAVEGAME_LOCATION="/home/steam/.local/share/Euro Truck Simulator 2/"
ARG EXECUTABLE="/app/bin/linux_x64/eurotrucks2_server"
ARG DEFAULT_PACKAGES="default_packages/ets2"

# This mapping is needed to have the variables available at runtime. Args are only for build time
ENV SAVEGAME_LOCATION="${SAVEGAME_LOCATION}"
ENV ETS_SERVER_CONFIG_FILE_PATH="${SAVEGAME_LOCATION}server_config.sii"
ENV EXECUTABLE=${EXECUTABLE}
ENV APP_ID=${APP_ID}

WORKDIR /app

USER root
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y python3 libatomic1 libx11-6 \
    && apt-get clean

# Create required dirs
RUN mkdir -p "${SAVEGAME_LOCATION}" \
    && chown steam:steam -R "${SAVEGAME_LOCATION}" \
    && mkdir -p /default_packages

COPY ets_server_entrypoint.py /ets_server_entrypoint.py
COPY entrypoint.sh /entrypoint
COPY VERSION /version
RUN chmod +x /entrypoint

COPY ["${DEFAULT_PACKAGES}/server_packages.dat", "/default_packages/"]
COPY ["${DEFAULT_PACKAGES}/server_packages.sii", "/default_packages/"]

USER steam

ENTRYPOINT [ "/entrypoint" ]
CMD [ "bash", "-c", "${EXECUTABLE}" ]

#!/bin/sh

set -e

# Copy default server_packages if they do not exist
cp -n /default_packages/server_packages.sii "${SAVEGAME_LOCATION}"
cp -n /default_packages/server_packages.dat "${SAVEGAME_LOCATION}"

# Generate config and update server
/usr/bin/python3 /ets_server_entrypoint.py

echo "[INFO]: Starting server..."
exec "$@"---README full---
# ETS2/ATS Convoy Multiplayer Dedicated Server
This docker container provides the new (as of Dec 2022) dedicated server for ETS2/ATS in a simple and complete package.  
Easy to configure and use!

# Contents
 - [Running](#running)
   - [ETS2](#ets2)
   - [ATS](#ats)
 - [Environment Variables](#environment-variables)
 - [Custom Mods](#custom-mods)
 - [Increase Max Player Limit above 8 Players](#increase-max-player-limit-above-8-players)
   - [Joining The Modified Server](#joining-the-modified-server)
 - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
   - [Login Error 15](#login-error-15)
   - [Login Error 106](#login-error-106)
   - [Can't write config file `server_config.sii`](#cant-write-config-file-server_configsii)
 - [Notes for development](#notes-for-development)
   - [Run tests after changes](#run-tests-after-changes)

# Running
## Minimal example:
### ETS2
```bash
docker run -d \
--name "ets2-server" \
--network host \
--restart unless-stopped \
-e "ETS_SERVER_NAME=My Server" \
lshallo/ets2-convoy-server
```
This minimal example will start the server with default settings and a custom name defined.  

To use your own config see [Mods](#custom-mods)

---
### ATS
```bash
docker run -d \
--name "ats-server" \
--network host \
--restart unless-stopped \
-e "ATS_SERVER_NAME=My Server" \
lshallo/ats-convoy-server
```
This minimal example will start the server with default settings and a custom name defined.  

To use your own config see [Mods](#custom-mods)


## Docker Compose
See [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml).

Then use `docker compose up -d` to start the server.  
You can check the logs with `docker compose logs -f`.

Update the server with `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`.
Stop the server with `docker compose stop` and remove it with `docker compose down`.

# Server Configuration
## Environment Variables
---
| Variable Name | Example | Description | Default |
| ---------------- | ------------------ | ----------------- | ---------- |
| ETS_SERVER_WRITE_CONFIG | true | Enable/disable automatic config generation from env variables. | true |
| ETS_SERVER_UPDATE_ON_START | true | Enable/disable update on server start. Will always update on first start to get server files. | true |
| ETS_SERVER_NAME | My Server | The name of the server. Shown ingame. | Euro Truck Simulator 2 Docker Server |
| ETS_SERVER_DESCRIPTION | Join me! | The description of the server. Shown ingame. | "" |
| ETS_SERVER_WELCOME_MESSAGE | Welcome to my server! | The welcome message. Shown ingame. | "" |
| ETS_SERVER_PASSWORD | password | The password required to join your server | "" |
| ETS_SERVER_MAX_PLAYERS | 8 | Max number of players. Can be hacked to support up to 128 | 8 |
| ETS_SERVER_MAX_VEHICLES_TOTAL | 100 | Maximum number of vehicles on server??? | 100 |
| ETS_SERVER_MAX_AI_VEHICLES_PLAYER | 50 | Maximum number of AI vehicles around a player??? | 50 |
| ETS_SERVER_MAX_AI_VEHICLES_PLAYER_SPAWN | 50 | ??? | 50 |
| ETS_SERVER_CONNECTION_VIRTUAL_PORT | 100 | Virtual connection port. Only used internally. Do not forward. | 100 |
| ETS_SERVER_QUERY_VIRTUAL_PORT | 101 | Virtual query port. Only used internally. Do not forward. | 101 |
| ETS_SERVER_PORT | 27015 | The external port of the server. You need to forward UDP + TCP. | 27015 |
| ETS_SERVER_QUERY_PORT | 27016 | The external query port of the server. You need to forward UDP + TCP. Must be in the range 27015 - 2720 for LAN games. | 27016 |
| ETS_SERVER_LOGON_TOKEN | 79gzbtepa2f0q72grfvazhhpsdasd | The logon token to have a persistent search token. See [Server README](ETS_SERVER_README.md#7-server-logon-token) | "" |
| ETS_SERVER_PLAYER_DAMAGE | true | Enable/disable player collisions | true |
| ETS_SERVER_TRAFFIC | true | Enable/disable traffic | true |
| ETS_SERVER_HIDE_IN_COMPANY | false | Enable/disable collisions of players in menu | false |
| ETS_SERVER_HIDE_COLLIDING | true | Enable/disable hiding of players in no collisions zone | true |
| ETS_SERVER_FORCE_SPEEDLIMITER | false | Enable/disable speed limit | false |
| ETS_SERVER_MODS_OPTIONING | false | Mark optional mods as required | false |
| ETS_SERVER_TIMEZONES | false | Enable time zones | false |
| ETS_SERVER_SERVICE_NO_COLLISION | false | Enable/disable collision in service areas (true = collisions enabled, false = collisions disabled) | false |
| ETS_SERVER_NAME_TAGS | true | Enable/disable display of name tags above trucks | true |
| ETS_SERVER_FRIENDS_ONLY | false | Limit server to steam friends??? | false |
| ETS_SERVER_SHOW_SERVER | true | Show server in public server list? | true |
| ETS_SERVER_MODERATORS | 208370238402, 2384723894723, 283947923 | List of steam IDs to turn moderatos on join. Moderators can alter the server time. See [Server README](ETS_SERVER_README.md#8-session-moderators) | "" |
| ETS_SERVER_CONFIG_FILE_PATH | /home/user/ets/server_config.sii | Path to server config file. | /home/steam/.local/share/Euro Truck Simulator 2/server_config.sii |
| ETS_SERVER_BRANCH | temporary_1_47 | Server branch. Allows downgrading to an older version. At SteamDB you'll find available branches for both [ETS2](https://steamdb.info/app/1948160/depots) and [ATS](https://steamdb.info/app/2239530/depots). To return back to the latest public release, use "public" | "" |

*Notes*:
- Variables are also supported with ATS_ prefix instead of ETS_
- Some are marked with question marks. I'm not sure what the parameters are doing. If you have any clue, please open an [issue](https://github.com/LsHallo/ets2-dedicated-convoy-server/issues) or [pull request](https://github.com/LsHallo/ets2-dedicated-convoy-server/pulls).


## Custom Mods
---
To enable your installed mods you need to generate custom `server_packages.dat` and `server_packages.sii` files.

1. Locate your ETS2 savegames folder
    - Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\Documents\Euro Truck Simulator 2`
    - Mac: 
        - No Steam Cloud: `~/Library/Application Support/Euro Truck Simulator 2/profiles/<Your Profile>/save`
        - Steam Cloud: `~/Library/Application Support/Steam/userdata/<Your ID>/304730/remote/profiles/<Your Profile>/save`
    - Linux: You know best ;)
  
  
2. Open `config.cfg` in your favourite editor (Notepad++, Emacs, Vim, ...)
    - Search for `uset g_console "0"` and replace it with `uset g_console "1"`
    - Search for `uset g_developer "0"` and replace it with `uset g_developer "1"`
    - Save the file

3. Start the game and load your desired save. The state (where your truck is) of the save is not important. We will only export mods.
    - Open the console by pressing the `~` key (left of 1 in the number row). It will vary depending on your keyboard layout.
    - Type `export_server_packages` in the console at the bottom of the screen and press enter.

4. Go to your savegames folder again.
    - You should see 2 new files: `server_packages.dat` and `server_packages.sii`
    - Copy the files to your ets2 server data directory (replacing the existing ones)
        - You need to mount `/home/steam/.local/share/Euro Truck Simulator 2` to a local directory using your docker run config.
        - Place the files in the mounted directory. E.g.: `/opt/ets2`
    - Restart your server

# Increase Max Player Limit above 8 Players

1. Set the desired player count using `ETS_SERVER_MAX_PLAYERS`
2. Start the container
3. Wait for the game to download and the server to start
4. Restart the container
5. You should see the server reporting: 
```
*** WARNING *** : [cvar] Can not create file '</home/steam/.local/share/Euro Truck Simulator 2 | /home>/config_ds.cfg'.
*** ERROR *** : [fs] Failed to open file '/home/config_ds.cfg' in the create_truncate mode.
[...]
*** WARNING *** : [MP] Warning: Proper player limit exceeded.
[...]
[MP] Maximum number of players: 32
```
Then the workaround is working.

### Joining the Modified Server
To join your modified server you'll need to set the same property also in your game.
First you need to enable developer mode: https://forum.scssoft.com/viewtopic.php?t=61852

Then in game press this key on your keyboard to open the console:  
![Keyboard](https://farm3.staticflickr.com/2840/10477930906_1ecf33ff78_o.png)

Enter `g_max_convoy_size 128` and press enter.
This setting is saved across reboots. However it might not survive updates and you might have to issue the command again.

Due to the hacky nature of the workaround I cannot provide any support.
Please don't create issues about it unless it prevents the server from starting at all.


# Troubleshooting


## Login Error 15
Login error 15 indicates that the token is for the wrong game. Please check that you have not used your ETS token for ATS or similar.  

See [ETS_SERVER_README.md](ETS_SERVER_README.md#7-server-logon-token) to genrate a new token.


## Login Error 106
Login error 106 indicates that your logon token is invalid.  
The token will lose validity after some time and you will need to generate a new one.  
To check if the token is still valid log into steam in a browser and go to [https://steamcommunity.com/dev/managegameservers](https://steamcommunity.com/dev/managegameservers).  
If the token has strike through it is no longer valid.  

See [ETS_SERVER_README.md](ETS_SERVER_README.md#7-server-logon-token) to genrate a new token.


## Can't write config file `server_config.sii`
Make sure the mounted folder owner is user id 1000.
`chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/ets2` (or whereever you have mounted it)


## Notes for development

### Run tests after changes
```shell
python -m unittest discover -s tests
```

This confirms my suspicion: entrypoint.sh copies default server_packages.sii and .dat files into the savegame location only if they don't already exist there, using "no clobber" copy behavior. So on first boot the container seeds vanilla default package files, but afterward leaves any existing customized versions untouched.

This means out of the box, without any customer file, the server successfully boots a working vanilla base-map convoy server. To use their own DLC or mods, customers need to export their own server_packages.sii/.dat from their game client, overwrite the defaults in the mounted save-data directory, and restart — which tells me the platform doesn't need a brand-new upload feature to support this workflow.

I need the investigation agent's report to confirm whether the file manager exposes the correct persistent directory and whether customers can already restart their servers from the dashboard. name: Docker Image CI

on:
  push:
    tags: [ "v*.*.*" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "master" ]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout the repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install unittest-xml-reporting

      - name: Run tests
        run: python -m xmlrunner discover -s tests -o test-results

      - name: Publish Test Report
        if: success() || failure()
        uses: mikepenz/action-junit-report@v6
        with:
          report_paths: test-results/*.xml

  build-ets2:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write

    steps:
      - name: Check out the repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Write VERSION file
        run: |
          touch VERSION
          echo "${{ github.ref_name || 'devel' }}" > VERSION
        shell: bash

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
      
      - name: Docker meta
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v6
        with:
          images: |
            lshallo/ets2-convoy-server
            ghcr.io/lshallo/ets2-convoy-server

      - name: Login to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        if: ${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' }}
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.registry_user }}
          password: ${{ secrets.registry_password }}

      - name: Login to Github Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        if: ${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' }}
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: ETS2 Convoy Server | Build and Push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: .
          file: ./Dockerfile
          push: ${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' }}
          platforms: linux/amd64
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}

  build-ats:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write

    steps:
      - name: Check out the repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Write VERSION file
        run: |
          touch VERSION
          echo "${{ github.ref_name || 'devel' }}" > VERSION
        shell: bash

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
      
      - name: Docker meta
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v6
        with:
          images: |
            lshallo/ats-convoy-server
            ghcr.io/lshallo/ats-convoy-server

      - name: Login to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        if: ${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' }}
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.registry_user }}
          password: ${{ secrets.registry_password }}

      - name: Login to Github Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        if: ${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' }}
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: ATS Convoy Server | Build and Push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: .
          file: ./Dockerfile
          push: ${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' }}
          build-args: |
            APP_ID=2239530
            SAVEGAME_LOCATION=/home/steam/.local/share/American Truck Simulator/
            EXECUTABLE=/app/bin/linux_x64/amtrucks_server
            DEFAULT_PACKAGES=default_packages/ats
          platforms: linux/amd64
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}---VERSION---

4	 * fabric/forge, see lib/game-config.ts's MINECRAFT.variants).
5	 *
6	 * Found live 2026-08-30: this substitution never existed anywhere in the
7	 * provisioning pipeline. The OsTemplate's setupScript is one static string
8	 * with no `TYPE` at all, so `gameVariant` was captured at checkout, stored on
9	 * `Server`, and then completely ignored — every Minecraft customer got plain
10	 * Vanilla regardless of what they picked (or paid for a plugin-support tier
11	 * and had their manually-installed plugins never load, since Vanilla has no
12	 * plugin API at all). Diagnosed via a real customer ticket: the fix here is
13	 * minecraft-specific by design (it's the only family with a real variant
14	 * concept today) — generalize via `schemaFor(family)` if another family gains
15	 * one, rather than hardcoding a second family name here.
16	 *
17	 * Explicit and idempotent: always injects a `TYPE`, even for "vanilla" —
18	 * removes any reliance on the image's own default ever staying Vanilla — and
19	 * is a no-op if the script already names an explicit `TYPE` (never override
20	 * something a future per-family script sets on purpose).
21	 *
22	 * Kept in its own side-effect-free module (rather than inline in
23	 * worker/index.ts) so it can be unit tested directly — importing
24	 * worker/index.ts runs its top-level `main()` job-polling loop.
25	 */
26	import { schemaFor, minecraftImageForVersion } from "../lib/game-config";
27	
28	export function applyGameVariant(setupScript: string, family: string | null, variant: string | null): string {
29	  if (family !== "minecraft") return setupScript;
30	  if (!variant) return setupScript;
31	  if (/-e\s+TYPE=/.test(setupScript)) return setupScript;
32	  const type = variant.toUpperCase();
33	  return setupScript.replace(/(docker run\s+(?:-d|--detach)\b)/, `$1 -e TYPE=${type}`);
34	}
35	
36	/**
37	 * Substitute the Minecraft image's Java-runtime tag to match the customer's
38	 * checkout-time VERSION choice.
39	 *
40	 * FOUND LIVE 2026-09-20: unlike every other customizable field, the
41	 * `itzg/minecraft-server` IMAGE TAG in `prisma/catalog.ts`'s setupScript is
42	 * not a `-e KEY=...` docker env var — it's the image reference itself — so
43	 * `applyGameConfigEnv` below (which only ever rewrites `-e KEY=` placeholders)
44	 * never touched it. Every Minecraft server was provisioned on the catalog's
45	 * static `:java21` regardless of the VERSION actually picked at checkout,
46	 * silently crash-looping any version needing a different Java (26.1+ needs
47	 * Java 25 — see lib/game-config.ts's MINECRAFT_JAVA_CUTOVERS for the real,
48	 * researched mapping and the live incident that found this).
49	 *
50	 * Deliberately minecraft-only and deliberately narrow: touches ONLY the
51	 * `itzg/minecraft-server(:tag)?` image reference, nothing else in the script.
52	 * Falls back to the schema's own VERSION default when the customer's
53	 * `gameConfig` doesn't carry one (an order that never touched the field) —
54	 * matching today's catalog default (1.21.1 -> java21) exactly, so a customer
55	 * who never touches VERSION sees no change in behavior.
56	 */
57	export function applyMinecraftJavaImage(
58	  setupScript: string,
59	  family: string | null,
60	  gameConfig: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined
61	): string {
62	  if (family !== "minecraft") return setupScript;
63	  if (!/itzg\/minecraft-server(:[\w.-]+)?/.test(setupScript)) return setupScript;
64	  const version = gameConfig && gameConfig["VERSION"] != null ? String(gameConfig["VERSION"]) : "1.21.1";
65	  const image = minecraftImageForVersion(version);
66	  return setupScript.replace(/itzg\/minecraft-server(:[\w.-]+)?/, image);
67	}
68	
69	/**
70	 * The generalization this file's own docstring called for: substitute a
71	 * customer's checkout-time `Server.gameConfig` values into an OsTemplate's
72	 * setupScript, for whichever fields already appear in it as a docker
73	 * `-e KEY=...` env-var placeholder.
74	 *
75	 * Found live 2026-08-31 auditing DST (`dst` family): the whole per-family
76	 * customization schema in lib/game-config.ts (`ConfigField`, one per
77	 * `docker run -e KEY=...` in prisma/seed-wave4-games.ts and its Wave 1-3
78	 * predecessors) is captured at checkout into `Server.gameConfig`
79	 * (lib/game-order.ts) and shown in the post-deploy Settings tab, but — same
80	 * root cause as `applyGameVariant` above, just never generalized —
81	 * `provision()` in worker/index.ts never read it. Every family's setup
82	 * script always ran with its hardcoded static default (usually `''`),
83	 * regardless of what the customer entered at checkout. For most fields that
84	 * meant a cosmetically-wrong default (wrong MOTD, wrong hostname string);
85	 * for DST's `TOKEN` (an online DST cluster refuses to start with none — see
86	 * lib/game-config.ts's DST schema comment) it meant the container never
87	 * bound its port at all and PROVISION's own `checkGamePortOpen` health check
88	 * would time out and hard-fail the customer's paid order.
89	 *
90	 * Deliberately conservative: ONLY touches a key if the setupScript already
91	 * declares it as `-e KEY=...` — fields with no such placeholder (e.g. DST's
92	 * `PASSWORD`, which the yeetzone image never wired to an env var at all) are
93	 * left untouched rather than guessing a docker flag that isn't there.
94	 * Values are re-quoted as a single-quoted shell literal with proper `'`
95	 * escaping (`'\''`) so a customer-supplied string can never break out of the
96	 * quote and inject shell — the same safety property `validateConfig`'s own
97	 * control-character guard exists for, just extended to this second consumer
98	 * (a `docker run` command line) since the injection surface differs from a
99	 * line-oriented remote config file.
100	 */
101	/**
102	 * Substitute a freshly generated per-server secret into an OsTemplate's
103	 * setupScript, for a family whose image needs a real secret value that the
104	 * static catalog row can only ever leave blank — baking one directly into
105	 * the shared seed string (prisma/catalog.ts) would hand every future
106	 * customer the exact SAME value, since that row is one string shared by
107	 * every server of that family.
108	 *
109	 * Found live 2026-09-05 fixing a customer's "player list never loads"
110	 * ticket: the platform's own player-list/RCON feature (lib/game-control.ts)
111	 * requires Palworld's ADMIN_PASSWORD to be set (it doubles as the RCON auth
112	 * secret) and RCON's port published, but the catalog's setupScript set
113	 * neither — so no Palworld server, ever provisioned, could support the
114	 * player-list feature customers are paying for. RCON_ENABLED/RCON_PORT are
115	 * not secrets, so those went directly into prisma/catalog.ts's setupScript
116	 * string; only this one per-server value needs runtime substitution.
117	 *
118	 * Same conservative shape as applyGameConfigEnv: only touches a key that's
119	 * already present as `-e KEY=...` in the script, and the caller decides what
120	 * counts as a "secret" for a given family — this function has no per-family
121	 * knowledge of its own.
122	 */
123	export function applyGameControlSecrets(
124	  setupScript: string,
125	  secrets: Record<string, string>,
126	): string {
127	  let out = setupScript;
128	  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(secrets)) {
129	    const re = new RegExp(`-e\\s+${key}=(?:'[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\\S*)`);
130	    if (!re.test(out)) continue;
131	    const escaped = value.replace(/'/g, `'\\''`);
132	    out = out.replace(re, `-e ${key}='${escaped}'`);
133	  }
134	  return out;
135	}
136	
137	export function applyGameConfigEnv(
138	  setupScript: string,
139	  family: string | null,
140	  gameConfig: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined,
141	): string {
142	  if (!family || !gameConfig) return setupScript;
143	  const schema = schemaFor(family);
144	  if (!schema) return setupScript;
145	  let out = setupScript;
146	  for (const field of schema.fields) {
147	    const raw = gameConfig[field.key];
148	    if (raw === undefined || raw === null) continue;
149	    // envKey lets a readable schema key (e.g. "world") differ from the
150	    // literal docker env var name the image expects (e.g. "WORLD_NAME") —
151	    // see ConfigField.envKey's doc comment in lib/game-config.ts.
152	    const envName = field.envKey ?? field.key;
153	    const re = new RegExp(`-e\\s+${envName}=(?:'[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\\S*)`);
154	    if (!re.test(out)) continue; // this field isn't docker-env-driven in this script — leave it alone
155	    const escaped = String(raw).replace(/'/g, `'\\''`);
156	    out = out.replace(re, `-e ${envName}='${escaped}'`);
157	  }
158	  return out;
159	}

1	/**
2	 * Per-game customization schema (MVP).
3	 *
4	 * A plain module (NO "use server") so it can be imported from server components,
5	 * "use server" action files AND the worker daemon alike — it holds no secrets and
6	 * performs no I/O.
7	 *
8	 * It declares, per game family, the available server *variants* (the loader/flavour
9	 * a player runs — Paper vs Vanilla, Carbon vs Oxide, …) and a versioned list of
10	 * *settings fields* that drive a dynamic UI. Fields are intentionally limited to
11	 * the handful of options players actually change, keyed on the game's own real
12	 * config keys (server.properties, PalWorldSettings.ini, cvars, …) — no invented
13	 * cvars — so a future real "apply" step can render them 1:1.
14	 *
15	 * Exports: `familyFor`, `schemaFor`, `validateConfig` plus the `GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS`
16	 * table and its types.
17	 */
18	
19	/** Bump when the field set changes in a way the worker/apply step must notice. */
20	export const GAME_CONFIG_VERSION = 1;
21	
22	export type FieldType = "enum" | "bool" | "int" | "string";
23	
24	/**
25	 * When a setting takes effect:
26	 *  - "deploy": needs a server restart / redeploy (world seed, tickrate, …)
27	 *  - "live":   can be pushed to a running server (motd, pvp, max players, …)
28	 * MVP treats both the same (simulated apply) but the UI surfaces the distinction.
29	 */
30	export type FieldPhase = "deploy" | "live";
31	
32	export type ConfigField = {
33	  /** The game's own config key (e.g. "max-players", "ServerPlayerMaxNum"). */
34	  key: string;
35	  label: string;
36	  /** UI grouping heading. */
37	  group: string;
38	  type: FieldType;
39	  default: string | number | boolean;
40	  /** enum only — {value,label} choices. */
41	  options?: { value: string; label: string }[];
42	  /**
43	   * enum only. When true and `options` is long, the settings UI renders a
44	   * type-to-filter combobox (components/customer/SearchableSelect.tsx)
45	   * instead of a plain native `<select>` — a flat dropdown of 100+ entries
46	   * has no usable way to find one. Leave unset for short option lists
47	   * (gamemode, difficulty, …), where a native select is simpler and fine.
48	   */
49	  searchable?: boolean;
50	  /** int only — inclusive bounds. */
51	  min?: number;
52	  max?: number;
53	  phase: FieldPhase;
54	  /** optional one-line helper shown under the field. */
55	  help?: string;
56	  /**
57	   * string fields only. When true, `validateConfig` rejects a blank value —
58	   * used for values with no sane platform default where the server is
59	   * genuinely non-functional / unjoinable without a customer-supplied
60	   * credential (e.g. DST's Klei cluster TOKEN — an online DST cluster
61	   * refuses to start at all without one). Enforced both at order-creation
62	   * time (lib/game-order.ts, BEFORE payment) and at settings-save time
63	   * (lib/actions-game-config.ts), so it gates checkout AND blocks a customer
64	   * from blanking it back out later. See DST.TOKEN below for the motivating
65	   * incident (added same-day as the family, 2026-08-31 audit).
66	   */
67	  required?: boolean;
68	  /**
69	   * Override the docker `-e KEY=` name that `applyGameConfigEnv`
70	   * (worker/game-variant.ts) substitutes into, when it differs from `key`.
71	   *
72	   * Found live 2026-09-11: Valheim's World Name field is keyed `"world"` (a
73	   * readable schema key, matches the game's own `-world` flag name) but the
74	   * lloesche/valheim-server image's actual env var is `WORLD_NAME`.
75	   * `applyGameConfigEnv` matches literally on `field.key`, so `-e world=`
76	   * never appeared in the setup script and the customer's chosen world name
77	   * was silently dropped at provisioning — every Valheim server booted on
78	   * the catalog's hardcoded default world regardless of what was ordered.
79	   * Set this whenever a field's readable schema key isn't the literal env
80	   * var name the image expects.
81	   */
82	  envKey?: string;
83	};
84	
85	export type GameVariant = {
86	  id: string;
87	  label: string;
88	  description?: string;
89	};
90	
91	export type FamilySchema = {
92	  family: string;
93	  label: string;
94	  variants: GameVariant[];
95	  defaultVariant: string;
96	  fields: ConfigField[];
97	};

99	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
100	// Minecraft version -> required Java runtime (itzg/minecraft-server image tag)
101	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
102	
103	/**
104	 * Minimum Java major version each range of Minecraft releases genuinely
105	 * needs, per Mojang's own real cutovers (minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorials/
106	 * Update_Java, confirmed live 2026-09-20). Sorted newest-cutover-first; the
107	 * first entry whose `min` is <= the target version wins.
108	 *
109	 * FOUND LIVE 2026-09-20: `worker/game-config.ts`'s MINECRAFT_IMAGE was a
110	 * single hardcoded `itzg/minecraft-server:java21` for every Minecraft server
111	 * regardless of chosen VERSION, and `prisma/catalog.ts`'s provisioning
112	 * setupScript baked the identical literal tag in directly — only the
113	 * `VERSION` env var itself was ever substituted per-customer
114	 * (`applyGameConfigEnv`), never the image. 26.1 and newer (offered below in
115	 * MINECRAFT_RELEASE_VERSIONS) requires Java 25; Java 21 cannot run it at all.
116	 * Confirmed live via server minecraft-qj4rxt (customer picked 26.2): `docker
117	 * logs mc` -> "Minecraft 26.1 and newer requires running the server with Java
118	 * 25 or above.", container never actually started, every existing health
119	 * check (GAME_UPDATE/GAME_POWER) saw only "the container/service object
120	 * exists" and never noticed.
121	 *
122	 * Checked itzg/docker-minecraft-server's own docs (docs/versions/java.md) for
123	 * whether the image can auto-select the right JDK from the requested
124	 * VERSION — it explicitly cannot: tags are static per-Java-version, and the
125	 * docs point at this same Minecraft-wiki table for the mapping rather than
126	 * doing it themselves. `latest`/`stable` DO auto-track whichever Java the
127	 * newest release needs (java25 today) — but floating with whatever Mojang
128	 * ships next is exactly the footgun already fixed here once, for the VERSION
129	 * field itself (the 2026-09-06 Cobblemon incident — see MINECRAFT.fields'
130	 * VERSION comment below): an unannounced future Java bump on those tags
131	 * could just as easily break an old pinned-version modded server. A pinned,
132	 * versioned cutover table — maintained by hand the same deliberate way this
133	 * file already tracks MINECRAFT_RELEASE_VERSIONS — is the safer "plug and
134	 * play" shape: deterministic per Minecraft VERSION, one line to add when
135	 * Mojang's next real cutover ships.
136	 *
137	 * All five `javaN` tags below were verified to genuinely exist 2026-09-20
138	 * against Docker Hub's own registry API (HTTP 200 on each of java25/java21/

content.thinking:
DST's TOKEN field is the pattern to follow, but for ETS2/ATS's SERVER_PACKAGES concept it should be `required: false` since vanilla works fine by default, with detailed help text explaining the SFTP path and export_server_packages steps — unlike DST which requires the token to start at all.

Actually, I need to question whether a string field is even right here versus pure documentation. Since applyGameConfigEnv works by substituting `-e KEY=VALUE` in the setup script, but server_packages.sii is binary file content rather than an env var string, this can't be a ConfigField with an envKey the same way — it's fundamentally a file, not a variable. So my job is to avoid faking a ConfigField for it and instead document clearly, likely in help text or a notes block, that customers need to use SFTP to drop in server_packages.sii/dat.

I'm also considering whether other "drop in your own content" games — like Valheim's world save or DayZ's maps — already have a UI mechanism for this kind of file-based setup that I could reuse, and I want to check the investigation results for that before deciding on marketing copy, provisioning help text, or a generic file-manager hint component.

content.thinking:
This CS16 example is a great precedent — the rconPassword field isn't exposed as a docker env var at all, left unset at provision time with help text pointing to SFTP configuration instead. That's the pattern for fields that can't be expressed as env vars: a ConfigField without envKey wiring.

But now I'm second-guessing whether it makes sense to add a purely informational field for something like server_packages.sii/dat that has zero effect via docker env and is already default behavior. The codebase's own ethos is "no invented cvars, keyed on the game's own real config keys" — and since this isn't even a key/value pair but a binary blob, forcing it into ConfigField feels inconsistent with that principle.

The rcon_password case is different since it maps to a real single-string cvar even if not wired through docker env, but "your own server_packages.sii" is an uploaded file, not a string value, so it doesn't belong as a ConfigField. I'm thinking the better path is documenting this elsewhere — in marketing copy, dashboard help banners, or catalog descriptions — and I want to check game-mods.ts, game-control.ts, and games.ts for existing notices mechanisms, plus the seed file and worker diff to see how this is handled elsewhere.

### 2. SFTP / file-manager infrastructure for customers (`/opt/nxeon`, production)

**Model.** There is one `Server` Prisma model (`prisma/schema.prisma` line 707) shared by plain VPS and every game-server product — a game server is just a `Server` row with an `osTemplate` pointing at a game family and a `gamePlan`. Customers get **root SSH/SFTP to the whole VM**, not a scoped/jailed account and not a per-container shell. There is no separate "SFTP user" provisioning step for game families: the same root password minted during VM provisioning (`worker/index.ts` line ~706/757, `generatePassword()` → `encryptSecret()` → `Server.rootPasswordEnc`) is reused for both the control-panel SSH card and the file manager.

**Core transport — `/opt/nxeon/lib/sftp.ts`** (full file read above, 524 lines). Exports `serverRootPassword()` (decrypts `rootPasswordEnc`, falls back to legacy plaintext `rootPassword`), `connectionTarget()` (dedicated-IP servers → their own IP:22; NAT servers → their node's `publicIp` + the server's forwarded `sshPort`), and `withSftp()` which opens a real `ssh2-sftp-client` connection as `root` with the resolved password and always closes it in `finally`. Typed ops: `listDir`, `statPath`, `readFileText`/`writeFileText` (capped, e.g. 1 MB), `mkdirPath`, `renamePath`, `removePath`, `chmodPath`, `readFileBuffer`/`writeFileBuffer` (streaming, used by the upload/download route). Path safety: `normalizePath()` rejects relative paths, `..` traversal, NUL bytes, overlong paths; `sanitizeUploadName()` strips all directory components from a client filename so an upload can only ever land inside the fixed `UPLOAD_DIR = "/root/nxeon-uploads"`. `SANDBOX` mode (staging, `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`) replaces every real SFTP call with an in-memory simulated filesystem per `server.id` — no real SSH connection opens on staging at all.

**Server actions — `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-files.ts`** (full file read above, 311 lines): `listFiles`, `readFile`, `saveFile`, `createFolder`, `renameEntry`, `deleteEntry`, `chmodEntry`, `uploadToServer` (base64 upload, hard-fixed to `UPLOAD_DIR`), `statEntry`. Every action re-derives the server via `ownedServer(serverId)` (`userId === caller` or `role === "ADMIN"`), rate-limits per user/op via `checkRateLimit`, and maps internal errors through `safeError()` so only path/size/ownership messages (never raw connection/protocol internals) reach the client.

**Route handler — `/opt/nxeon/app/api/files/[serverId]/route.ts`** (full file read above): `GET ?path=&download=1` streams a file (`readFileBuffer`, forces `Content-Disposition: attachment`); `POST ?path=` accepts a multipart upload (up to 250 MB) and writes via `writeFileBuffer`, best-effort `mkdirPath`ing the target dir first. Both ownership-checked and rate-limited independently of the server actions above.

**Two backends, one component.** `/opt/nxeon/lib/files-types.ts` defines the `FileApi` interface (`list/read/save/mkdir/rename/remove/uploadUrl/downloadUrl?/chmod?`) that the file-manager UI is written against. `/opt/nxeon/lib/files-adapters.ts` provides `serverFileApi(serverId)` (wraps `lib/actions-files.ts`, absolute root-VM paths — this is what game servers use) and `hostingFileApi(accountId, root)` (wraps `lib/actions-hosting-fs.ts` for the separate chrooted shared-hosting product). This is genuinely a real SFTP client talking to the customer's own VM as root — **not** a shell-into-container mechanism; a game running inside a Docker container just happens to have its data bind-mounted at a host path like `/opt/cs16` or `/opt/armareforger` (per `GAME_CONTROL.dataRoots`), which the root SFTP session can browse like any other host directory.

**UI.** `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/files/FileBrowser.tsx` (`ServerFileBrowser`, 467 lines) — a three-pane browser (lazy-loaded folder tree, listing, inline editor for small text-ish files under 1 MB) plus `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/files/UploadQueue.tsx` (219 lines, XHR-based multi-file upload queue hitting `uploadUrl`). Mounted in `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` at both the "Files" tab (line 600, `gameFilesPanel`) and the VPS "Files" tab (line 615, `filesPanel`) — same component, gated on `server.status === "RUNNING"`. Separately, `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/SftpAccess.tsx` (full file read above) renders a read-only credentials card (host/port/username `root`/password + ready-to-copy `sftp -P <port> root@<host>` and `ssh -p <port> root@<host>` command strings) so a customer can also point FileZilla/WinSCP/Cyberduck/OpenSSH directly at the box — this is shown on both the VPS Settings tab (line ~1422) and specifically called out as "the game branch" in a comment at line 877.

**Precedent for "drop in your own content" already exists platform-wide.** Marketing copy across many existing families explicitly tells customers to use file/FTP access to add their own content — e.g. `app/(marketing)/satisfactory-server-hosting/page.tsx` ("upload an existing save directly instead of starting fresh"), `app/(marketing)/ark-server-hosting/page.tsx` ("Full FTP file access lets you upload mods and edit GameUserSettings.ini/Game.ini"), `app/(marketing)/rust-server-hosting/page.tsx` ("upload custom maps, drop in plugins, hand-edit server.cfg"), `app/(marketing)/minecraft-server-hosting/page.tsx`, `mordhau-server-hosting/page.tsx`, `tf2-server-hosting/page.tsx`, and the generic per-family template generators `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts` (lines ~552, 572, 809: "full file access means you can use it fully, or upload your own configs and mods") and `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` (lines ~529, 546, 991). This confirms the file manager is the platform's established, load-bearing answer to "how does a customer get their own content onto the server" — it is not a new concept to introduce.

### 3. Precedent: something lands on a server's filesystem as part of an async job

**`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-mods.ts`** (full 376-line file read above) is the canonical example.

- **Queueing**: `installMod(serverId, modId)` / `uninstallMod(serverId, modId)` are `"use server"` actions. Each: authenticates + ownership-checks via `ownedServer()`, validates the mod against the server's family/variant, checks `hasInflightJob()` (`db.job.count({ where: { serverId, status: { in: ["QUEUED","RUNNING"] } } })` — enforces one in-flight job per server), upserts a `ServerMod` row to `status: "INSTALLING"` (or `"REMOVING"`), then `await db.job.create({ data: { type: "GAME_MOD_SYNC", serverId } })`. State lives in the DB row, not the job payload — "the same state-driven pattern as GAME_CONFIG (worker reads the DB, no per-op payloads to trust)" per the file's own header comment.
- **Prisma models** (`prisma/schema.prisma`): `Job` (line 1071: `id, type: JobType, status: JobStatus, payload: Json?, error, progress, step, attempts, serverId, createdAt, updatedAt`), `GameMod` (line 2944: the catalog — `gameFamily, name, slug, category, source, sourceId, url, modStringId, appliesToVariant, ...` plus a large block of upstream-verified metadata), `ServerMod` (line 3104: the per-server install-state join row — `serverId, modId, status ("INSTALLING"|"INSTALLED"|"FAILED"|"REMOVING"|"REMOVED"), version, error`, unique on `[serverId, modId]`).
- **Worker pickup**: `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts`'s main loop (lines 3183–3208) polls `db.job.findFirst({ where: { status: "QUEUED" }, orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" } })`, then atomically claims it with `db.job.updateMany({ where: { id, status: "QUEUED" }, data: { status: "RUNNING", attempts: increment } })` (count===1 wins the race), then dispatches via a flat `handlers: Record<string, (job: Job) => Promise<void>>` map (line 2215) — `GAME_MOD_SYNC: gameModSync` (line 2243).
- **Handler — `/opt/nxeon/worker/game-mods.ts`** (full 1000-line file read above): `gameModSync(job)` loads the server + all pending `ServerMod` rows, then branches three ways: `SANDBOX` (simulate only), `!REAL_ENABLED` (mark `FAILED` with an honest "not applied yet" message — never fakes success), or the real path. The real path is one of:
  - **Direct download installs** (`modrinth`, `spigotmc`, `umod`, `thunderstore`, `github`): resolve a direct download URL from the source's API (`resolveUrl()`), then open a plain SSH exec session (`withSsh`/`execRemote`, root@VM, same password source as the file manager via `connectionTarget`/`serverRootPassword` from `lib/sftp.ts`) and have the **VM itself `curl` the file** into a deterministic path computed by `modDirShell()` (e.g. Minecraft's `plugins`/`mods` dir found via `find`, or Valheim's fixed `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins`). Uninstall is a plain `rm`.
  - **Steam Workshop installs** (`workshopSync` → per-family `applyXWorkshop` functions, ~600 lines): never downloads/mirrors the Workshop item itself. Either (a) writes the desired Workshop-ID list into a container env var and does a full stop/rename/recreate/verify/rollback container cycle (`recreateContainer`, lines 581–624 — systemd-unit-aware, rolls back to the `-old` container on failure) — used for ARK/DST/Squad/Soulmask; or (b) runs Valve's own `steamcmd` **once inside the customer's own container** (`docker exec <container> steamcmd +login anonymous ...`) to pull the item from Steam's CDN, then writes it into place over an SFTP channel (`withSftp`/`sftpWrite`, e.g. `applyL4d2Workshop` fetching `.vpk`s into `/opt/l4d2/addons/`, or `applyEmpyrionWorkshop` copying a fetched scenario into `Content/Scenarios/` and rewriting `dedicated.yaml`).
- **This is directly relevant precedent** for "place something onto a server's filesystem as part of an async job": the mechanism is always (1) a `Job` row with `type` + `serverId`, no trusted payload, (2) desired-state recorded on a DB row the worker reconciles toward, (3) file placement done either by SSH `exec` (`curl`/`docker exec steamcmd`) or by an SFTP channel opened with the exact same root-password auth as the customer-facing file manager — there's no separate "internal" transport.

**Free Minecraft tier (`freemc`) — a different, synchronous pattern, not a job queue.** Files found: `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-mods.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-roles.ts`, `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-public.ts`, `lib/freemc-mod-catalog.ts`, `lib/freemc-command-catalog.ts`, `lib/freemc-capacity.ts`, `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx` + `components/customer/freemc/v2/FreeMcHero.tsx`. **There is no `worker/freemc*.ts` file** — grepping `worker/*.ts` for "freemc"/"FreeMinecraft" returns nothing. Every freemc action (`switchFreeMinecraftGameType`, `applyFreeMinecraftGameMode`, `applyFreeMinecraftMods`, etc., all read in full above) does its work **synchronously inside the "use server" action itself**, via `lib/ssh-exec.ts`'s `withServerSsh`/`exec`/`shellQuote` helpers, against a single shared `freemc-host` VM (`db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" } })`) — never a `db.job.create`. The pattern per-user is: one Docker container per customer on the shared host, isolated by `-e LEVEL=<gameType>` and a per-user data path (`/opt/freemc/servers/<freeMinecraftServerId>`); switching game type / applying mods / mode is a full `docker rm -f` + `docker run -d` **container recreate** (`recreateGameTypeContainer` in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`) with an explicit roll-back-to-previous-config step on failure (mirrored in both `actions-freemc-worlds.ts` and `actions-freemc-mods.ts`). Content (extra plugins) is added purely by setting the `MODRINTH_PROJECTS` env var wider — `itzg/minecraft-server`'s own entrypoint does the actual download inside the container on boot; **Nxeon never writes a customer-supplied file into a freemc container** anywhere in these files. I did not find any freemc code path that stages/writes an arbitrary file before or during provisioning — mods/presets/inventory/roles are all env-var or RCON-driven, not file-drop.

### 2. SFTP / file-manager infrastructure for customers (`/opt/nxeon`, production)

**Model.** There is one `Server` Prisma model (`prisma/schema.prisma` line 707) shared by plain VPS and every game-server product — a game server is just a `Server` row with an `osTemplate` pointing at a game family and a `gamePlan`. Customers get **root SSH/SFTP to the whole VM**, not a scoped/jailed account and not a per-container shell. There is no separate "SFTP user" provisioning step for game families: the same root password minted during VM provisioning (`worker/index.ts` line ~706/757, `generatePassword()` → `encryptSecret()` → `Server.rootPasswordEnc`) is reused for both the control-panel SSH card and the file manager.

**Core transport — `/opt/nxeon/lib/sftp.ts`** (full file read above, 524 lines). Exports `serverRootPassword()` (decrypts `rootPasswordEnc`, falls back to legacy plaintext `rootPassword`), `connectionTarget()` (dedicated-IP servers → their own IP:22; NAT servers → their node's `publicIp` + the server's forwarded `sshPort`), and `withSftp()` which opens a real `ssh2-sftp-client` connection as `root` with the resolved password and always closes it in `finally`. Typed ops: `listDir`, `statPath`, `readFileText`/`writeFileText` (capped, e.g. 1 MB), `mkdirPath`, `renamePath`, `removePath`, `chmodPath`, `readFileBuffer`/`writeFileBuffer` (streaming, used by the upload/download route). Path safety: `normalizePath()` rejects relative paths, `..` traversal, NUL bytes, overlong paths; `sanitizeUploadName()` strips all directory components from a client filename so an upload can only ever land inside the fixed `UPLOAD_DIR = "/root/nxeon-uploads"`. `SANDBOX` mode (staging, `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`) replaces every real SFTP call with an in-memory simulated filesystem per `server.id` — no real SSH connection opens on staging at all.

**Server actions — `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-files.ts`** (full file read above, 311 lines): `listFiles`, `readFile`, `saveFile`, `createFolder`, `renameEntry`, `deleteEntry`, `chmodEntry`, `uploadToServer` (base64 upload, hard-fixed to `UPLOAD_DIR`), `statEntry`. Every action re-derives the server via `ownedServer(serverId)` (`userId === caller` or `role === "ADMIN"`), rate-limits per user/op via `checkRateLimit`, and maps internal errors through `safeError()` so only path/size/ownership messages (never raw connection/protocol internals) reach the client.

**Route handler — `/opt/nxeon/app/api/files/[serverId]/route.ts`** (full file read above): `GET ?path=&download=1` streams a file (`readFileBuffer`, forces `Content-Disposition: attachment`); `POST ?path=` accepts a multipart upload (up to 250 MB) and writes via `writeFileBuffer`, best-effort `mkdirPath`ing the target dir first. Both ownership-checked and rate-limited independently of the server actions above.

**Two backends, one component.** `/opt/nxeon/lib/files-types.ts` defines the `FileApi` interface (`list/read/save/mkdir/rename/remove/uploadUrl/downloadUrl?/chmod?`) that the file-manager UI is written against. `/opt/nxeon/lib/files-adapters.ts` provides `serverFileApi(serverId)` (wraps `lib/actions-files.ts`, absolute root-VM paths — this is what game servers use) and `hostingFileApi(accountId, root)` (wraps `lib/actions-hosting-fs.ts` for the separate chrooted shared-hosting product). This is genuinely a real SFTP client talking to the customer's own VM as root — **not** a shell-into-container mechanism; a game running inside a Docker container just happens to have its data bind-mounted at a host path like `/opt/cs16` or `/opt/armareforger` (per `GAME_CONTROL.dataRoots`), which the root SFTP session can browse like any other host directory.

**UI.** `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/files/FileBrowser.tsx` (`ServerFileBrowser`, 467 lines) — a three-pane browser (lazy-loaded folder tree, listing, inline editor for small text-ish files under 1 MB) plus `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/files/UploadQueue.tsx` (219 lines, XHR-based multi-file upload queue hitting `uploadUrl`). Mounted in `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` at both the "Files" tab (line 600, `gameFilesPanel`) and the VPS "Files" tab (line 615, `filesPanel`) — same component, gated on `server.status === "RUNNING"`. Separately, `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/SftpAccess.tsx` (full file read above) renders a read-only credentials card (host/port/username `root`/password + ready-to-copy `sftp -P <port> root@<host>` and `ssh -p <port> root@<host>` command strings) so a customer can also point FileZilla/WinSCP/Cyberduck/OpenSSH directly at the box — this is shown on both the VPS Settings tab (line ~1422) and specifically called out as "the game branch" in a comment at line 877.

**Precedent for "drop in your own content" already exists platform-wide.** Marketing copy across many existing families explicitly tells customers to use file/FTP access to add their own content — e.g. `app/(marketing)/satisfactory-server-hosting/page.tsx` ("upload an existing save directly instead of starting fresh"), `app/(marketing)/ark-server-hosting/page.tsx` ("Full FTP file access lets you upload mods and edit GameUserSettings.ini/Game.ini"), `app/(marketing)/rust-server-hosting/page.tsx` ("upload custom maps, drop in plugins, hand-edit server.cfg"), `app/(marketing)/minecraft-server-hosting/page.tsx`, `mordhau-server-hosting/page.tsx`, `tf2-server-hosting/page.tsx`, and the generic per-family template generators `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts` (lines ~552, 572, 809: "full file access means you can use it fully, or upload your own configs and mods") and `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` (lines ~529, 546, 991). ### 3. Precedent: something lands on a server's filesystem as part of an async job

**`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-mods.ts`** (full 376-line file read above) is the canonical example.

- **Queueing**: `installMod(serverId, modId)` / `uninstallMod(serverId, modId)` are `"use server"` actions. Each: authenticates + ownership-checks via `ownedServer()`, validates the mod against the server's family/variant, checks `hasInflightJob()` (`db.job.count({ where: { serverId, status: { in: ["QUEUED","RUNNING"] } } })` — enforces one in-flight job per server), upserts a `ServerMod` row to `status: "INSTALLING"` (or `"REMOVING"`), then `await db.job.create({ data: { type: "GAME_MOD_SYNC", serverId } })`. State lives in the DB row, not the job payload — "the same state-driven pattern as GAME_CONFIG (worker reads the DB, no per-op payloads to trust)" per the file's own header comment.
- **Prisma models** (`prisma/schema.prisma`): `Job` (line 1071: `id, type: JobType, status: JobStatus, payload: Json?, error, progress, step, attempts, serverId, createdAt, updatedAt`), `GameMod` (line 2944: the catalog — `gameFamily, name, slug, category, source, sourceId, url, modStringId, appliesToVariant, ...` plus a large block of upstream-verified metadata), `ServerMod` (line 3104: the per-server install-state join row — `serverId, modId, status ("INSTALLING"|"INSTALLED"|"FAILED"|"REMOVING"|"REMOVED"), version, error`, unique on `[serverId, modId]`).
- **Worker pickup**: `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts`'s main loop (lines 3183–3208) polls `db.job.findFirst({ where: { status: "QUEUED" }, orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" } })`, then atomically claims it with `db.job.updateMany({ where: { id, status: "QUEUED" }, data: { status: "RUNNING", attempts: increment } })` (count===1 wins the race), then dispatches via a flat `handlers: Record<string, (job: Job) => Promise<void>>` map (line 2215) — `GAME_MOD_SYNC: gameModSync` (line 2243).
- **Handler — `/opt/nxeon/worker/game-mods.ts`** (full 1000-line file read above): `gameModSync(job)` loads the server + all pending `ServerMod` rows, then branches three ways: `SANDBOX` (simulate only), `!REAL_ENABLED` (mark `FAILED` with an honest "not applied yet" message — never fakes success), or the real path. The real path is one of:
  - **Direct download installs** (`modrinth`, `spigotmc`, `umod`, `thunderstore`, `github`): resolve a direct download URL from the source's API (`resolveUrl()`), then open a plain SSH exec session (`withSsh`/`execRemote`, root@VM, same password source as the file manager via `connectionTarget`/`serverRootPassword` from `lib/sftp.ts`) and have the **VM itself `curl` the file** into a deterministic path computed by `modDirShell()` (e.g. Minecraft's `plugins`/`mods` dir found via `find`, or Valheim's fixed `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins`). Uninstall is a plain `rm`.
  - **Steam Workshop installs** (`workshopSync` → per-family `applyXWorkshop` functions, ~600 lines): never downloads/mirrors the Workshop item itself. Either (a) writes the desired Workshop-ID list into a container env var and does a full stop/rename/recreate/verify/rollback container cycle (`recreateContainer`, lines 581–624 — systemd-unit-aware, rolls back to the `-old` container on failure) — used for ARK/DST/Squad/Soulmask; or (b) runs Valve's own `steamcmd` **once inside the customer's own container** (`docker exec <container> steamcmd +login anonymous ...`) to pull the item from Steam's CDN, then writes it into place over an SFTP channel (`withSftp`/`sftpWrite`, e.g. `applyL4d2Workshop` fetching `.vpk`s into `/opt/l4d2/addons/`, or `applyEmpyrionWorkshop` copying a fetched scenario into `Content/Scenarios/` and rewriting `dedicated.yaml`).
- **This is directly relevant precedent** for "place something onto a server's filesystem as part of an async job": the mechanism is always (1) a `Job` row with `type` + `serverId`, no trusted payload, (2) desired-state recorded on a DB row the worker reconciles toward, (3) file placement done either by SSH `exec` (`curl`/`docker exec steamcmd`) or by an SFTP channel opened with the exact same root-password auth as the customer-facing file manager — there's no separate "internal" transport.

**Free Minecraft tier (`freemc`) — a different, synchronous pattern, not a job queue.** Files found: `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-mods.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-roles.ts`, `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-public.ts`, `lib/freemc-mod-catalog.ts`, `lib/freemc-command-catalog.ts`, `lib/freemc-capacity.ts`, `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx` + `components/customer/freemc/v2/FreeMcHero.tsx`. **There is no `worker/freemc*.ts` file** — grepping `worker/*.ts` for "freemc"/"FreeMinecraft" returns nothing. Every freemc action (`switchFreeMinecraftGameType`, `applyFreeMinecraftGameMode`, `applyFreeMinecraftMods`, etc., all read in full above) does its work **synchronously inside the "use server" action itself**, via `lib/ssh-exec.ts`'s `withServerSsh`/`exec`/`shellQuote` helpers, against a single shared `freemc-host` VM (`db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" } })`) — never a `db.job.create`. The pattern per-user is: one Docker container per customer on the shared host, isolated by `-e LEVEL=<gameType>` and a per-user data path (`/opt/freemc/servers/<freeMinecraftServerId>`); switching game type / applying mods / mode is a full `docker rm -f` + `docker run -d` **container recreate** (`recreateGameTypeContainer` in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`) with an explicit roll-back-to-previous-config step on failure (mirrored in both `actions-freemc-worlds.ts` and `actions-freemc-mods.ts`). Content (extra plugins) is added purely by setting the `MODRINTH_PROJECTS` env var wider — `itzg/minecraft-server`'s own entrypoint does the actual download inside the container on boot; **Nxeon never writes a customer-supplied file into a freemc container** anywhere in these files. I did not find any freemc code path that stages/writes an arbitrary file before or during provisioning — mods/presets/inventory/roles are all env-var or RCON-driven, not file-drop.

### 2. SFTP / file-manager infrastructure for customers (`/opt/nxeon`, production)

**Model.** There is one `Server` Prisma model (`prisma/schema.prisma` line 707) shared by plain VPS and every game-server product — a game server is just a `Server` row with an `osTemplate` pointing at a game family and a `gamePlan`. Customers get **root SSH/SFTP to the whole VM**, not a scoped/jailed account and not a per-container shell. There is no separate "SFTP user" provisioning step for game families: the same root password minted during VM provisioning (`worker/index.ts` line ~706/757, `generatePassword()` → `encryptSecret()` → `Server.rootPasswordEnc`) is reused for both the control-panel SSH card and the file manager.

**Core transport — `/opt/nxeon/lib/sftp.ts`** (full file read above, 524 lines). Exports `serverRootPassword()` (decrypts `rootPasswordEnc`, falls back to legacy plaintext `rootPassword`), `connectionTarget()` (dedicated-IP servers → their own IP:22; NAT servers → their node's `publicIp` + the server's forwarded `sshPort`), and `withSftp()` which opens a real `ssh2-sftp-client` connection as `root` with the resolved password and always closes it in `finally`. Typed ops: `listDir`, `statPath`, `readFileText`/`writeFileText` (capped, e.g. 1 MB), `mkdirPath`, `renamePath`, `removePath`, `chmodPath`, `readFileBuffer`/`writeFileBuffer` (streaming, used by the upload/download route). Path safety: `normalizePath()` rejects relative paths, `..` traversal, NUL bytes, overlong paths; `sanitizeUploadName()` strips all directory components from a client filename so an upload can only ever land inside the fixed `UPLOAD_DIR = "/root/nxeon-uploads"`. `SANDBOX` mode (staging, `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`) replaces every real SFTP call with an in-memory simulated filesystem per `server.id` — no real SSH connection opens on staging at all.

**Server actions — `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-files.ts`** (full file read above, 311 lines): `listFiles`, `readFile`, `saveFile`, `createFolder`, `renameEntry`, `deleteEntry`, `chmodEntry`, `uploadToServer` (base64 upload, hard-fixed to `UPLOAD_DIR`), `statEntry`. Every action re-derives the server via `ownedServer(serverId)` (`userId === caller` or `role === "ADMIN"`), rate-limits per user/op via `checkRateLimit`, and maps internal errors through `safeError()` so only path/size/ownership messages (never raw connection/protocol internals) reach the client.

**Route handler — `/opt/nxeon/app/api/files/[serverId]/route.ts`** (full file read above): `GET ?path=&download=1` streams a file (`readFileBuffer`, forces `Content-Disposition: attachment`); `POST ?path=` accepts a multipart upload (up to 250 MB) and writes via `writeFileBuffer`, best-effort `mkdirPath`ing the target dir first. Both ownership-checked and rate-limited independently of the server actions above.

**Two backends, one component.** `/opt/nxeon/lib/files-types.ts` defines the `FileApi` interface (`list/read/save/mkdir/rename/remove/uploadUrl/downloadUrl?/chmod?`) that the file-manager UI is written against. `/opt/nxeon/lib/files-adapters.ts` provides `serverFileApi(serverId)` (wraps `lib/actions-files.ts`, absolute root-VM paths — this is what game servers use) and `hostingFileApi(accountId, root)` (wraps `lib/actions-hosting-fs.ts` for the separate chrooted shared-hosting product). This is genuinely a real SFTP client talking to the customer's own VM as root — **not** a shell-into-container mechanism; a game running inside a Docker container just happens to have its data bind-mounted at a host path like `/opt/cs16` or `/opt/armareforger` (per `GAME_CONTROL.dataRoots`), which the root SFTP session can browse like any other host directory.

**UI.** `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/files/FileBrowser.tsx` (`ServerFileBrowser`, 467 lines) — a three-pane browser (lazy-loaded folder tree, listing, inline editor for small text-ish files under 1 MB) plus `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/files/UploadQueue.tsx` (219 lines, XHR-based multi-file upload queue hitting `uploadUrl`). Mounted in `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` at both the "Files" tab (line 600, `gameFilesPanel`) and the VPS "Files" tab (line 615, `filesPanel`) — same component, gated on `server.status === "RUNNING"`. Separately, `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/SftpAccess.tsx` (full file read above) renders a read-only credentials card (host/port/username `root`/password + ready-to-copy `sftp -P <port> root@<host>` and `ssh -p <port> root@<host>` command strings) so a customer can also point FileZilla/WinSCP/Cyberduck/OpenSSH directly at the box — this is shown on both the VPS Settings tab (line ~1422) and specifically called out as "the game branch" in a comment at line 877.

**Precedent for "drop in your own content" already exists platform-wide.** Marketing copy across many existing families explicitly tells customers to use file/FTP access to add their own content — e.g. `app/(marketing)/satisfactory-server-hosting/page.tsx` ("upload an existing save directly instead of starting fresh"), `app/(marketing)/ark-server-hosting/page.tsx` ("Full FTP file access lets you upload mods and edit GameUserSettings.ini/Game.ini"), `app/(marketing)/rust-server-hosting/page.tsx` ("upload custom maps, drop in plugins, hand-edit server.cfg"), `app/(marketing)/minecraft-server-hosting/page.tsx`, `mordhau-server-hosting/page.tsx`, `tf2-server-hosting/page.tsx`, and the generic per-family template generators `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts` (lines ~552, 572, 809: "full file access means you can use it fully, or upload your own configs and mods") and `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` (lines ~529, 546, 991). This confirms the file manager is the platform's established, load-bearing answer to "how does a customer get their own content onto the server" — it is not a new concept to introduce.

### 3. Precedent: something lands on a server's filesystem as part of an async job

**`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-mods.ts`** (full 376-line file read above) is the canonical example.

- **Queueing**: `installMod(serverId, modId)` / `uninstallMod(serverId, modId)` are `"use server"` actions. Each: authenticates + ownership-checks via `ownedServer()`, validates the mod against the server's family/variant, checks `hasInflightJob()` (`db.job.count({ where: { serverId, status: { in: ["QUEUED","RUNNING"] } } })` — enforces one in-flight job per server), upserts a `ServerMod` row to `status: "INSTALLING"` (or `"REMOVING"`), then `await db.job.create({ data: { type: "GAME_MOD_SYNC", serverId } })`. State lives in the DB row, not the job payload — "the same state-driven pattern as GAME_CONFIG (worker reads the DB, no per-op payloads to trust)" per the file's own header comment.
- **Prisma models** (`prisma/schema.prisma`): `Job` (line 1071: `id, type: JobType, status: JobStatus, payload: Json?, error, progress, step, attempts, serverId, createdAt, updatedAt`), `GameMod` (line 2944: the catalog — `gameFamily, name, slug, category, source, sourceId, url, modStringId, appliesToVariant, ...` plus a large block of upstream-verified metadata), `ServerMod` (line 3104: the per-server install-state join row — `serverId, modId, status ("INSTALLING"|"INSTALLED"|"FAILED"|"REMOVING"|"REMOVED"), version, error`, unique on `[serverId, modId]`).
- **Worker pickup**: `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts`'s main loop (lines 3183–3208) polls `db.job.findFirst({ where: { status: "QUEUED" }, orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" } })`, then atomically claims it with `db.job.updateMany({ where: { id, status: "QUEUED" }, data: { status: "RUNNING", attempts: increment } })` (count===1 wins the race), then dispatches via a flat `handlers: Record<string, (job: Job) => Promise<void>>` map (line 2215) — `GAME_MOD_SYNC: gameModSync` (line 2243).
- **Handler — `/opt/nxeon/worker/game-mods.ts`** (full 1000-line file read above): `gameModSync(job)` loads the server + all pending `ServerMod` rows, then branches three ways: `SANDBOX` (simulate only), `!REAL_ENABLED` (mark `FAILED` with an honest "not applied yet" message — never fakes success), or the real path. The real path is one of:
  - **Direct download installs** (`modrinth`, `spigotmc`, `umod`, `thunderstore`, `github`): resolve a direct download URL from the source's API (`resolveUrl()`), then open a plain SSH exec session (`withSsh`/`execRemote`, root@VM, same password source as the file manager via `connectionTarget`/`serverRootPassword` from `lib/sftp.ts`) and have the **VM itself `curl` the file** into a deterministic path computed by `modDirShell()` (e.g. Minecraft's `plugins`/`mods` dir found via `find`, or Valheim's fixed `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins`). Uninstall is a plain `rm`.
  - **Steam Workshop installs** (`workshopSync` → per-family `applyXWorkshop` functions, ~600 lines): never downloads/mirrors the Workshop item itself. Either (a) writes the desired Workshop-ID list into a container env var and does a full stop/rename/recreate/verify/rollback container cycle (`recreateContainer`, lines 581–624 — systemd-unit-aware, rolls back to the `-old` container on failure) — used for ARK/DST/Squad/Soulmask; or (b) runs Valve's own `steamcmd` **once inside the customer's own container** (`docker exec <container> steamcmd +login anonymous ...`) to pull the item from Steam's CDN, then writes it into place over an SFTP channel (`withSftp`/`sftpWrite`, e.g. `applyL4d2Workshop` fetching `.vpk`s into `/opt/l4d2/addons/`, or `applyEmpyrionWorkshop` copying a fetched scenario into `Content/Scenarios/` and rewriting `dedicated.yaml`).
- **This is directly relevant precedent** for "place something onto a server's filesystem as part of an async job": the mechanism is always (1) a `Job` row with `type` + `serverId`, no trusted payload, (2) desired-state recorded on a DB row the worker reconciles toward, (3) file placement done either by SSH `exec` (`curl`/`docker exec steamcmd`) or by an SFTP channel opened with the exact same root-password auth as the customer-facing file manager — there's no separate "internal" transport.

**Free Minecraft tier (`freemc`) — a different, synchronous pattern, not a job queue.** Files found: `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-mods.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-roles.ts`, `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-public.ts`, `lib/freemc-mod-catalog.ts`, `lib/freemc-command-catalog.ts`, `lib/freemc-capacity.ts`, `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx` + `components/customer/freemc/v2/FreeMcHero.tsx`. **There is no `worker/freemc*.ts` file** — grepping `worker/*.ts` for "freemc"/"FreeMinecraft" returns nothing. Every freemc action (`switchFreeMinecraftGameType`, `applyFreeMinecraftGameMode`, `applyFreeMinecraftMods`, etc., all read in full above) does its work **synchronously inside the "use server" action itself**, via `lib/ssh-exec.ts`'s `withServerSsh`/`exec`/`shellQuote` helpers, against a single shared `freemc-host` VM (`db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" } })`) — never a `db.job.create`. The pattern per-user is: one Docker container per customer on the shared host, isolated by `-e LEVEL=<gameType>` and a per-user data path (`/opt/freemc/servers/<freeMinecraftServerId>`); switching game type / applying mods / mode is a full `docker rm -f` + `docker run -d` **container recreate** (`recreateGameTypeContainer` in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`) with an explicit roll-back-to-previous-config step on failure (mirrored in both `actions-freemc-worlds.ts` and `actions-freemc-mods.ts`). Content (extra plugins) is added purely by setting the `MODRINTH_PROJECTS` env var wider — `itzg/minecraft-server`'s own entrypoint does the actual download inside the container on boot; **Nxeon never writes a customer-supplied file into a freemc container** anywhere in these files. I did not find any freemc code path that stages/writes an arbitrary file before or during provisioning — mods/presets/inventory/roles are all env-var or RCON-driven, not file-drop.
