input.content:
/**
 * Wave 11 games — make Euro Truck Simulator 2 and American Truck Simulator
 * (SCS Software's "Convoy" dedicated multiplayer) orderable. Same Docker/
 * OsTemplate pattern as every prior wave: a community Docker image (wrapping
 * anonymous SteamCMD) installed by the OsTemplate.setupScript in cloud-init,
 * reusing the existing generic worker/game-control.ts + lib/game-control.ts
 * machinery. No worker/index.ts changes were needed — unlike Palworld/Rust/
 * CS2/Arma Reforger, this game has no RCON/admin-console protocol and no
 * secret that needs minting at provision time (see lib/game-config.ts's
 * Wave 11 header).
 *
 * PROVENANCE — re-investigating the Wave 10 blocker (2026-09-24): Wave 10
 * (prisma/seed-wave10-games.ts) positively researched ETS2/ATS and declined
 * to ship them, concluding "the dedicated server cannot start with real
 * content until the CUSTOMER uploads a server_packages.sii/.dat pair... a
 * file-upload checkout flow this platform doesn't have yet". That conclusion
 * was reached from SCS's own wiki alone (modding.scssoft.com/wiki/
 * Documentation/Tools/Dedicated_Server — "these files are necessary for a
 * dedicated server to start") WITHOUT checking whether the actual chosen
 * Docker image papers over that requirement. It does: LsHallo/
 * ets2-dedicated-convoy-server's Dockerfile (fetched raw off
 * raw.githubusercontent.com, not summarized) COPIES a baked-in
 * `default_packages/<ets2|ats>/server_packages.{sii,dat}` pair into the image
 * at build time, and entrypoint.sh runs `cp -n /default_packages/... "$SAVE"`
 * (no-clobber) on every container start. Consequence: the server boots and
 * hosts a fully working VANILLA base-map convoy with ZERO customer file,
 * immediately, on first order. A customer who owns paid DLC maps or wants
 * mods active still needs their OWN exported server_packages.sii/.dat (SCS's
 * own wiki: "these files are NOT linked to your account in any way" — there
 * is no way to fabricate a valid one for a specific customer's DLC/mod
 * ownership) — but getting it onto the server needs NOTHING new: this
 * platform's existing root SFTP/file-manager access (lib/sftp.ts,
 * lib/actions-files.ts, components/customer/files/FileBrowser.tsx) already
 * reaches the exact host directory (`/opt/ets2` / `/opt/ats`, bind-mounted
 * below) the container reads those files from — identical shape to how
 * ark/rust/satisfactory/mordhau/tf2 etc. already tell customers to add their
 * own maps/mods/saves over the same file manager (see lib/game-mods.ts's
 * `ets2`/`ats` MOD_INFO entries for the customer-facing instructions, and
 * lib/game-config.ts's Wave 11 header for the fuller citation trail — SCS's
 * wiki, SCS's own "Server config paramaters" field list, and the Docker
 * image's README/Dockerfile/entrypoint.sh/docker-compose.yml/GitHub Actions
 * build matrix, all fetched live, none recalled from memory).
 *
 * Steam App IDs (the GAME's own client app, needed for a customer's own
 * Steam Logon Token per lib/game-config.ts's server_logon_token field — NOT
 * the dedicated-server tool's app id, which is a different, easy-to-confuse
 * number SCS's own wiki explicitly warns not to use for this):
 *   ets2  227300   (client) — dedicated server tool is a SEPARATE app,
 *                    1948160, confirmed via SCS's own wiki "How to download
 *                    a dedicated server" section (Steam library tools list).
 *   ats   270880   (client) — dedicated server tool is 2239530, same wiki
 *                    section.
 * Both server tools install via anonymous SteamCMD (no GSLT, no game
 * ownership required to run the dedicated server binary itself — confirmed
 * by Wave 10's own research spike, re-confirmed here against the same wiki).
 *
 * Docker images: lshallo/ets2-convoy-server and lshallo/ats-convoy-server
 * (GitHub: LsHallo/ets2-dedicated-convoy-server, MIT-adjacent Apache-2.0,
 * 79 stars / 12 forks, 50k+ Docker Hub pulls, latest tag v0.4.6 pushed
 * ~2026-07 and still being actively pulled daily — a real, maintained
 * community image). Both images are built off the SAME repo/Dockerfile via a
 * GitHub Actions build matrix that only varies APP_ID/SAVEGAME_LOCATION/
 * EXECUTABLE/DEFAULT_PACKAGES per game (fetched raw off
 * .github/workflows/docker-image.yml) — confirms the env-var surface and
 * default-packages behavior are identical between the two, just re-prefixed
 * ETS_/ATS_.
 *
 * Volume: `/opt/<family>` is bind-mounted to the image's own documented
 * save-data path (`/home/steam/.local/share/Euro Truck Simulator 2` for
 * ets2, `/home/steam/.local/share/American Truck Simulator` for ats — note
 * the literal space in both container-side paths; quoted as a single `-v`
 * argument, which Docker's short `host:container` syntax accepts fine since
 * it splits on the first colon, not on whitespace). `chown -R 1000:1000` on
 * the host directory before first start is REQUIRED per the image's own
 * README troubleshooting section ("Can't write config file `server_config.
 * sii`... Make sure the mounted folder owner is user id 1000") — this
 * image's non-root `steam` user is uid 1000 (confirmed off the Dockerfile:
 * `USER steam`, base image `cm2network/steamcmd:steam`), a DIFFERENT
 * requirement from Arma Reforger's own image (uid >= 10000) in Wave 10 — not
 * copy-pasted from it.
 *
 * Ports: SCS's own wiki ("Ports setup" section) is explicit that BOTH
 * connection_dedicated_port (default 27015, the actual join port) and
 * query_dedicated_port (default 27016) need BOTH TCP and UDP forwarded for a
 * server behind NAT. All 4 combos are published below and wired into
 * lib/games.ts's GAME_PORT/GAME_EXTRA_JOIN_PORTS so the platform's own
 * generic NAT auto-forwarding (worker/index.ts's provision(), driven off
 * lib/ipam.ts's allocateGameForward) forwards every one of them automatically
 * — no bespoke per-family forwarding code was added.
 *
 * max_players is hard-capped at 8 across every tier — SCS's own real,
 * officially-supported ceiling (see lib/game-config.ts's field comment for
 * the "why", including the unsupported client-hack workaround this
 * deliberately does NOT offer as a paid upsell). All 3 tiers below therefore
 * differ only in RAM headroom for DLC maps/mods/AI traffic, not player count
 * — reflected in the tier names/blurbs rather than implying more RAM buys
 * more players.
 *
 * Pricing researched against real competitors (2026-09-24): Servers4Gamers
 * from $1.50/mo, Cybrancee from $3.99/mo, 4NetPlayers from ~$3.07/mo,
 * RespawnHost's fixed 2GB "Small Convoy" package from €6/mo (~$6.50).
 * RAM baseline from SCS's own forum (forum.scssoft.com/viewtopic.php?t=
 * 316296): the dedicated server process idles under 200MB RAM.
 *
 * NOT YET REAL-TEST-PROVISIONED (2026-09-24): same honest limitation as
 * Wave 10's own header — a real end-to-end Proxmox test provision (real VM
 * clone, real allocateIp/allocateSshPort/syncPortForwardsBestEffort) was not
 * attempted from this session: it requires production Proxmox/DB
 * credentials, which a background session should not obtain on its own
 * without explicit human sign-off (this repo's own CLAUDE.md: /opt/nxeon is
 * LIVE PRODUCTION). What WAS verified: `applyGameConfigEnv` (the real
 * function, worker/game-variant.ts) run directly against both setupScripts
 * below with distinctive test values for every field, confirming every
 * `envKey` substitutes correctly (see the worktree's own verify script /
 * commit message for the exact run); full `npm run check` (tsc --noEmit +
 * the entire test suite) passing with zero regressions; and the port/
 * dataRoots wiring cross-checked by hand against lib/ipam.ts's
 * allocateGameForward and worker/index.ts's provision() (both read in full,
 * not guessed at). Both OsTemplate rows are seeded here so a human (or an
 * interactive session with real credentials) can run this seed against
 * staging/prod and do that real test provision — do not treat this wave as
 * customer-ready until that happens once per family.
 *
 * Run: cd /opt/nxeon-staging && npx tsx prisma/seed-wave11-games.ts   (idempotent)
 */
import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";

const db = new PrismaClient();

type Template = { family: string; name: string; setupScript: string; minRamMB: number; minDiskGB: number };

const TEMPLATES: Template[] = [
  {
    family: "ets2", name: "Euro Truck Simulator 2 Server", minRamMB: 1024, minDiskGB: 10,
    setupScript: `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && mkdir -p /opt/ets2 && chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/ets2 && docker run -d --name ets2 --restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 30 -p 27015:27015 -p 27015:27015/udp -p 27016:27016 -p 27016:27016/udp -e ETS_SERVER_NAME='Nxeon ETS2 Convoy' -e ETS_SERVER_DESCRIPTION='' -e ETS_SERVER_WELCOME_MESSAGE='' -e ETS_SERVER_PASSWORD='' -e ETS_SERVER_MAX_PLAYERS='8' -e ETS_SERVER_PLAYER_DAMAGE='true' -e ETS_SERVER_TRAFFIC='true' -e ETS_SERVER_FORCE_SPEEDLIMITER='false' -e ETS_SERVER_NAME_TAGS='true' -e ETS_SERVER_LOGON_TOKEN='' -e ETS_SERVER_MODERATORS='' -v "/opt/ets2:/home/steam/.local/share/Euro Truck Simulator 2" lshallo/ets2-convoy-server:latest`,
  },
  {
    family: "ats", name: "American Truck Simulator Server", minRamMB: 1024, minDiskGB: 10,
    setupScript: `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && mkdir -p /opt/ats && chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/ats && docker run -d --name ats --restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 30 -p 27015:27015 -p 27015:27015/udp -p 27016:27016 -p 27016:27016/udp -e ATS_SERVER_NAME='Nxeon ATS Convoy' -e ATS_SERVER_DESCRIPTION='' -e ATS_SERVER_WELCOME_MESSAGE='' -e ATS_SERVER_PASSWORD='' -e ATS_SERVER_MAX_PLAYERS='8' -e ATS_SERVER_PLAYER_DAMAGE='true' -e ATS_SERVER_TRAFFIC='true' -e ATS_SERVER_FORCE_SPEEDLIMITER='false' -e ATS_SERVER_NAME_TAGS='true' -e ATS_SERVER_LOGON_TOKEN='' -e ATS_SERVER_MODERATORS='' -v "/opt/ats:/home/steam/.local/share/American Truck Simulator" lshallo/ats-convoy-server:latest`,
  },
];

type TierSpec = { gameFamily: string; name: string; ramMB: number; cpuCores: number; diskGB: number; slots: number; priceCents: number; featured?: boolean };

const TIERS: TierSpec[] = [
  // Euro Truck Simulator 2 — all 3 tiers cap at 8 players (SCS's real
  // ceiling); differ only in RAM headroom for DLC maps/mods. Pricing
  // neighborhood from real competitors researched above.
  { gameFamily: "ets2", name: "ETS2 — 1 GB / 8 players (Solo Convoy)", ramMB: 1024, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 10, slots: 8, priceCents: 299 },
  { gameFamily: "ets2", name: "ETS2 — 2 GB / 8 players (Standard Convoy)", ramMB: 2048, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 12, slots: 8, priceCents: 499, featured: true },
  { gameFamily: "ets2", name: "ETS2 — 4 GB / 8 players (Modded Convoy)", ramMB: 4096, cpuCores: 2, diskGB: 15, slots: 8, priceCents: 799 },

  // American Truck Simulator — identical shape/pricing to ETS2 (same
  // dedicated-server codebase, same real-world hosting-market pricing).
  { gameFamily: "ats", name: "ATS — 1 GB / 8 players (Solo Convoy)", ramMB: 1024, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 10, slots: 8, priceCents: 299 },
  { gameFamily: "ats", name: "ATS — 2 GB / 8 players (Standard Convoy)", ramMB: 2048, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 12, slots: 8, priceCents: 499, featured: true },
  { gameFamily: "ats", name: "ATS — 4 GB / 8 players (Modded Convoy)", ramMB: 4096, cpuCores: 2, diskGB: 15, slots: 8, priceCents: 799 },
];

async function main() {
  const templateIdByFamily = new Map<string, string>();
  let sort = 140;
  for (const t of TEMPLATES) {
    const os = await db.osTemplate.upsert({
      where: { slug: t.family },
      create: {
        slug: t.family, name: t.name, category: "APPLICATION", family: t.family, version: "", logo: t.family,
        vmid: 9000, baseVmid: 9000, setupScript: t.setupScript, minRamMB: t.minRamMB, minDiskGB: t.minDiskGB,
        licenseRequired: false, featured: false, sortOrder: sort++, active: true,
      },
      update: { name: t.name, setupScript: t.setupScript, minRamMB: t.minRamMB, minDiskGB: t.minDiskGB, active: true },
    });
    templateIdByFamily.set(t.family, os.id);
    console.log(`  osTemplate ${t.family.padEnd(16)} → ${os.id}`);
  }

  const plans = await db.plan.findMany({ where: { active: true }, orderBy: { ramMB: "asc" } });
  if (plans.length === 0) throw new Error("No active VPS plans — run the main seed first.");
  const largest = plans[plans.length - 1];

  let created = 0, updated = 0;
  const sortByGame = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const spec of TIERS) {
    const basePlan = plans.find((p) => p.ramMB >= spec.ramMB) ?? largest;
    const osId = templateIdByFamily.get(spec.gameFamily) ?? null;
    const sortOrder = sortByGame.get(spec.gameFamily) ?? 0;
    sortByGame.set(spec.gameFamily, sortOrder + 1);
    const data = {
      gameFamily: spec.gameFamily, name: spec.name, ramMB: spec.ramMB, cpuCores: spec.cpuCores, diskGB: spec.diskGB,
      slots: spec.slots, priceCents: spec.priceCents, termMonths: 1, basePlanId: basePlan.id, osTemplateId: osId,
      featured: spec.featured ?? false, active: true, sortOrder,
    };
    const existing = await db.gamePlan.findFirst({ where: { gameFamily: spec.gameFamily, name: spec.name } });
    if (existing) { await db.gamePlan.update({ where: { id: existing.id }, data }); updated++; }
    else { await db.gamePlan.create({ data }); created++; }
    console.log(`  plan ${spec.name.padEnd(42)} base=${basePlan.name}`);
  }
  console.log(`\nWave 11: ${TEMPLATES.length} OsTemplates, GamePlans ${created} created / ${updated} updated.`);
}

main().catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); }).finally(() => db.$disconnect());

import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";

const db = new PrismaClient();

type Template = { family: string; name: string; setupScript: string; minRamMB: number; minDiskGB: number };

const TEMPLATES: Template[] = [
  {
    family: "ets2", name: "Euro Truck Simulator 2 Server", minRamMB: 1024, minDiskGB: 10,
    setupScript: `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && mkdir -p /opt/ets2 && chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/ets2 && docker run -d --name ets2 --restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 30 -p 27015:27015 -p 27015:27015/udp -p 27016:27016 -p 27016:27016/udp -e ETS_SERVER_NAME='Nxeon ETS2 Convoy' -e ETS_SERVER_DESCRIPTION='' -e ETS_SERVER_WELCOME_MESSAGE='' -e ETS_SERVER_PASSWORD='' -e ETS_SERVER_MAX_PLAYERS='8' -e ETS_SERVER_PLAYER_DAMAGE='true' -e ETS_SERVER_TRAFFIC='true' -e ETS_SERVER_FORCE_SPEEDLIMITER='false' -e ETS_SERVER_NAME_TAGS='true' -e ETS_SERVER_LOGON_TOKEN='' -e ETS_SERVER_MODERATORS='' -v "/opt/ets2:/home/steam/.local/share/Euro Truck Simulator 2" lshallo/ets2-convoy-server:latest`,
  },
  {
    family: "ats", name: "American Truck Simulator Server", minRamMB: 1024, minDiskGB: 10,
    setupScript: `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && mkdir -p /opt/ats && chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/ats && docker run -d --name ats --restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 30 -p 27015:27015 -p 27015:27015/udp -p 27016:27016 -p 27016:27016/udp -e ATS_SERVER_NAME='Nxeon ATS Convoy' -e ATS_SERVER_DESCRIPTION='' -e ATS_SERVER_WELCOME_MESSAGE='' -e ATS_SERVER_PASSWORD='' -e ATS_SERVER_MAX_PLAYERS='8' -e ATS_SERVER_PLAYER_DAMAGE='true' -e ATS_SERVER_TRAFFIC='true' -e ATS_SERVER_FORCE_SPEEDLIMITER='false' -e ATS_SERVER_NAME_TAGS='true' -e ATS_SERVER_LOGON_TOKEN='' -e ATS_SERVER_MODERATORS='' -v "/opt/ats:/home/steam/.local/share/American Truck Simulator" lshallo/ats-convoy-server:latest`,
  },
];

type TierSpec = { gameFamily: string; name: string; ramMB: number; cpuCores: number; diskGB: number; slots: number; priceCents: number; featured?: boolean };

const TIERS: TierSpec[] = [
  // Euro Truck Simulator 2 — all 3 tiers cap at 8 players (SCS's real
  // ceiling); differ only in RAM headroom for DLC maps/mods. Pricing
  // neighborhood from real competitors researched above.
  { gameFamily: "ets2", name: "ETS2 — 1 GB / 8 players (Solo Convoy)", ramMB: 1024, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 10, slots: 8, priceCents: 299 },
  { gameFamily: "ets2", name: "ETS2 — 2 GB / 8 players (Standard Convoy)", ramMB: 2048, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 12, slots: 8, priceCents: 499, featured: true },
  { gameFamily: "ets2", name: "ETS2 — 4 GB / 8 players (Modded Convoy)", ramMB: 4096, cpuCores: 2, diskGB: 15, slots: 8, priceCents: 799 },

  // American Truck Simulator — identical shape/pricing to ETS2 (same
  // dedicated-server codebase, same real-world hosting-market pricing).
  { gameFamily: "ats", name: "ATS — 1 GB / 8 players (Solo Convoy)", ramMB: 1024, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 10, slots: 8, priceCents: 299 },
  { gameFamily: "ats", name: "ATS — 2 GB / 8 players (Standard Convoy)", ramMB: 2048, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 12, slots: 8, priceCents: 499, featured: true },
  { gameFamily: "ats", name: "ATS — 4 GB / 8 players (Modded Convoy)", ramMB: 4096, cpuCores: 2, diskGB: 15, slots: 8, priceCents: 799 },
];

async function main() {
  const templateIdByFamily = new Map<string, string>();
  let sort = 140;
  for (const t of TEMPLATES) {
    const os = await db.osTemplate.upsert({
      where: { slug: t.family },
      create: {
        slug: t.family, name: t.name, category: "APPLICATION", family: t.family, version: "", logo: t.family,
        vmid: 9000, baseVmid: 9000, setupScript: t.setupScript, minRamMB: t.minRamMB, minDiskGB: t.minDiskGB,
        licenseRequired: false, featured: false, sortOrder: sort++, active: true,
      },
      update: { name: t.name, setupScript: t.setupScript, minRamMB: t.minRamMB, minDiskGB: t.minDiskGB, active: true },
    });
    templateIdByFamily.set(t.family, os.id);
    console.log(`  osTemplate ${t.family.padEnd(16)} → ${os.id}`);
  }

  const plans = await db.plan.findMany({ where: { active: true }, orderBy: { ramMB: "asc" } });
  if (plans.length === 0) throw new Error("No active VPS plans — run the main seed first.");
  const largest = plans[plans.length - 1];

  let created = 0, updated = 0;
  const sortByGame = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const spec of TIERS) {
    const basePlan = plans.find((p) => p.ramMB >= spec.ramMB) ?? largest;
    const osId = templateIdByFamily.get(spec.gameFamily) ?? null;
    const sortOrder = sortByGame.get(spec.gameFamily) ?? 0;
    sortByGame.set(spec.gameFamily, sortOrder + 1);
    const data = {
      gameFamily: spec.gameFamily, name: spec.name, ramMB: spec.ramMB, cpuCores: spec.cpuCores, diskGB: spec.diskGB,
      slots: spec.slots, priceCents: spec.priceCents, termMonths: 1, basePlanId: basePlan.id, osTemplateId: osId,
      featured: spec.featured ?? false, active: true, sortOrder,
    };
    const existing = await db.gamePlan.findFirst({ where: { gameFamily: spec.gameFamily, name: spec.name } });
    if (existing) { await db.gamePlan.update({ where: { id: existing.id }, data }); updated++; }
    else { await db.gamePlan.create({ data }); created++; }
    console.log(`  plan ${spec.name.padEnd(42)} base=${basePlan.name}`);
  }
  console.log(`\nWave 11: ${TEMPLATES.length} OsTemplates, GamePlans ${created} created / ${updated} updated.`);
}

main().catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); }).finally(() => db.$disconnect());

+  Palworld) rather than exposed as a checkout field that would silently get discarded.

+  AMX Mod X), 3 GamePlan tiers (1GB/16p $3.99, 2GB/24p $5.99, 3GB/32p $7.99) — the cheapest slot-for-slot
+  family in the whole catalog. Every schema field carries an explicit `envKey` (the image's real env
+  vars are UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, don't match the natural camelCase schema keys) — the exact V-Rising-bug
+  class this wave was briefed to avoid repeating.

+vars were independently re-verified live via WebFetch against their own GitHub READMEs (not just
+recalled from the earlier research) — this resolved two of the research's own "NEEDS VERIFICATION"

+ambiguity the research raised), and CS 1.6's RCON_PASSWORD is confirmed genuinely absent from the
+image's env surface (left un-set rather than faked). GitHub API also confirmed a real staleness gap on

+`jsknnr/arma-reforger-server` at 2026-01-19) — flagged honestly in `prisma/seed-wave10-games.ts` rather

+build an in-house image on.

+correctly refused the step this required (copying `/opt/nxeon/.env` into the test worktree —

+infrastructure credentials on its own initiative. **This is a real, load-bearing gap, not a formality**:

+`npx tsx prisma/seed-wave10-games.ts` against `/opt/nxeon-staging` (or prod, per the normal promote
+flow), places one real order per family, and confirms the container starts and the join port opens —
+exactly the same one-time validation every prior wave (1-9) already did live before shipping.

+  DayZ-owning Steam account (still true, `lib/games.ts`'s pre-existing `arkasa` comment already
+  documented this), PLUS two newly-identified blockers — DayZ configures via `serverDZ.cfg` + launch
+  params, not docker env vars (no `envKey` schema mapping applies at all), and the Steam EULA for app
+  223350 literally says non-commercial-use-only (an unenforced industry-wide norm, but a real distinct
+  risk worth an explicit owner sign-off). Needs a real engineering spike, not a schema/seed change.
+- **ETS2 + American Truck Simulator** — positively researched (Linux-native, anonymous SteamCMD,
+  confirmed app IDs 1948160/2239530, no GSLT) but not scaffolded: the dedicated server cannot start with
+  real content until the customer uploads a `server_packages.sii`/`.dat` pair their own local game
+  client generates — a file-upload checkout flow this platform doesn't have yet.
+- **RuneScape / World of Warcraft** — owner-DECLINED (reverse-engineered emulators of the developer's
+  own proprietary server-side logic, sustained real litigation history from both Jagex and Blizzard) —
+  a deliberate exclusion, not an oversight.
+- **PUBG** — left pending (no confirmed official dedicated-server product existed at research time).
+- **StarRupture** — the disclosed RCE flagged during the original research was never confirmed patched
+  upstream; not added.

+- **Hytale, SCUM, HumanitZ, VEIN** — researched by the other 3 agents in this same batch but outside
+  this session's explicit approve/decline list; left for a follow-up pass rather than guessed at.

## Wave 11 — Euro Truck Simulator 2 + American Truck Simulator (2026-09-24)

Two new orderable game families, built on branch `feature/ets2-ats-truck-sim` in the worktree
`/opt/nxeon-staging-ets2ats` (never built in the live `/opt/nxeon` tree). **Not merged, not deployed,
not seeded into any database** — a human reviews and promotes.

**The actual blocker, corrected.** Wave 10 (`prisma/seed-wave10-games.ts`) positively researched
ETS2/ATS and declined to ship them: "the dedicated server cannot start with real content until the
customer uploads a `server_packages.sii`/`.dat` pair their own local game client generates — a
file-upload checkout flow this platform doesn't have yet." That conclusion came from SCS Software's own
wiki alone (modding.scssoft.com/wiki/Documentation/Tools/Dedicated_Server — "these files are necessary
for a dedicated server to start") **without checking whether the chosen Docker image papers over that
requirement.** It does: `LsHallo/ets2-dedicated-convoy-server`'s `Dockerfile` (fetched raw, not
summarized) `COPY`s a baked-in `default_packages/<ets2|ats>/server_packages.{sii,dat}` pair into the
image at build time, and `entrypoint.sh` runs `cp -n /default_packages/... "$SAVEGAME_LOCATION"`
(no-clobber) on every container start. **The server boots and hosts a fully working vanilla base-map
convoy with zero customer file, immediately, on first order.**

A customer who owns paid DLC maps or wants mods active still needs their own exported
`server_packages.sii`/`.dat` (SCS's own wiki: "these files are NOT linked to your account in any way" —
there is no way to fabricate a valid one for a specific customer's DLC/mod ownership) — but getting it
onto the server needs **nothing new**. This platform's existing root SFTP/file-manager access
(`lib/sftp.ts`, `lib/actions-files.ts`, `components/customer/files/FileBrowser.tsx`, already reachable
from the customer dashboard's Files tab) reaches the exact host directory (`/opt/ets2` / `/opt/ats`,
bind-mounted by `prisma/seed-wave11-games.ts`'s setupScript) the container reads those files from —
identical shape to how ark/rust/satisfactory/mordhau/tf2/plutonium already tell customers to add their
own maps/mods/saves over the same file manager (confirmed by reading their marketing-page copy — this
is an established, live platform pattern, not something invented for this wave). No new upload feature,
no new job type, no new Prisma model. `lib/game-mods.ts`'s `ets2`/`ats` `MOD_INFO` entries carry the
customer-facing instructions (export via the game's own console command, then SFTP both files into
place and restart) — worth noting honestly: `MOD_INFO` itself is not currently rendered anywhere in the
live UI (confirmed by grepping every `.tsx` for the import — zero hits, platform-wide, for every
family, not just these two), so today the ONLY place a customer sees this is the marketing page's FAQ
(the same channel the ark/rust/satisfactory precedent already relies on) — a real, pre-existing,
platform-wide discoverability gap worth a future fix, not something this wave introduced or needed to
solve.

**Shipped:** `lib/games.ts`/`lib/game-config.ts`/`lib/game-control.ts` entries for both families, real
Steam CDN key art (`public/games/art/ets2_*.jpg` / `ats_*.jpg`, sourced from each title's own CLIENT
app id — 227300 ETS2, 270880 ATS, NOT the dedicated-server tool's app ids 1948160/2239530 — nominative
product-ID use), `app/(marketing)/euro-truck-simulator-2-server-hosting/page.tsx` and
`.../american-truck-simulator-server-hosting/page.tsx`, `lshallo/ets2-convoy-server` +
`lshallo/ats-convoy-server` Docker images (79 stars, 50k+ pulls, actively maintained), 3 GamePlan tiers
each (1GB $2.99, 2GB $4.99 popular, 4GB $7.99 — all capped at 8 players, SCS's own real ceiling, tiers
differ only in RAM headroom for DLC/mods). Every schema field carries an explicit `envKey` mapping the
game's own `server_config.sii` field name (`lobby_name`, `max_players`, `server_logon_token`, …) to the
Docker image's literal `-e ETS_SERVER_*`/`-e ATS_SERVER_*` name, same discipline as Valheim's
`world`/`WORLD_NAME`. No `worker/index.ts` changes were needed — unlike Palworld/Rust/CS2/Arma
Reforger, this game has no RCON/admin-console protocol at all and no secret to mint at provision time.

**Verified this session:** `applyGameConfigEnv` (the real function, `worker/game-variant.ts`) run
directly against both real setupScripts with 11 distinctive test-marker values per family (22 total) —
every `envKey` substituted correctly, and a negative control confirmed the original default values were
genuinely replaced, not left in place by a no-op regex. TypeScript typecheck: 0 errors (every
`Record<GameFamily, …>` exhaustiveness site was already covered — no missed call sites this time). Full
test suite: 1422 tests, identical 40 pre-existing failures before and after (diffed the exact failing
test names between this branch and the untouched `feature/new-game-families-arma-cs16` reference
worktree — byte-for-byte the same 40, all unrelated billing/proration/auth/rate-limiting tests, none
touching a file this wave modified), 0 regressions.

**NOT verified — a real end-to-end Proxmox test provision was not attempted**, for the same reason as
Wave 10: it requires production Proxmox/database credentials that a background session should not
obtain on its own without explicit human sign-off (this repo's own `CLAUDE.md`: `/opt/nxeon` is LIVE
PRODUCTION). What was checked instead, by reading the real code rather than guessing: `lib/ipam.ts`'s
`allocateGameForward`/`allocateIp`/`allocateSshPort` and `worker/index.ts`'s `provision()` (both read in
full) confirm the generic NAT auto-forwarding path needs no new code for these families — `lib/games.ts`'s
`GAME_PORT`/`GAME_EXTRA_JOIN_PORTS` entries alone drive it, and were built deliberately to avoid the
existing "admin-port retraction" path entirely (join port === health-check port, unlike rust/ark/etc.)
so there is no risk of the platform later deleting a forward this game genuinely needs. The concrete
next step is unchanged from Wave 10's own playbook: a human (or an interactive session with explicit
credential access) runs `npx tsx prisma/seed-wave11-games.ts` against staging/prod, places one real
order per family, and confirms the container starts (it should — and should already be joinable with
zero setup, since this image ships a working default), then confirms the SFTP-drop-in-DLC path works
end to end for a second, mod-owning order.

**Files touched:** `lib/games.ts`, `lib/game-config.ts`, `lib/game-control.ts`, `lib/game-mods.ts`,
`lib/game-player-recommend.ts`, `lib/game-update-verify.ts`, `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts`,
`components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx`, `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`, `app/sitemap.ts`,
`app/(marketing)/euro-truck-simulator-2-server-hosting/page.tsx`,
`app/(marketing)/american-truck-simulator-server-hosting/page.tsx`, `prisma/seed-wave11-games.ts`,
`public/games/art/ets2_{hero,poster}.jpg`, `public/games/art/ats_{hero,poster}.jpg`. `worker/index.ts`
was deliberately NOT touched (see above).

---

*Companion docs: `CLAUDE.md` (agent/ops conventions), `ROADMAP.md` (backlog), `docs/MIGRATION.md`
(server migration).*

not seeded into any database** — a human reviews and promotes.

**The actual blocker, corrected.** Wave 10 (`prisma/seed-wave10-games.ts`) positively researched
ETS2/ATS and declined to ship them: "the dedicated server cannot start with real content until the
customer uploads a `server_packages.sii`/`.dat` pair their own local game client generates — a
file-upload checkout flow this platform doesn't have yet." That conclusion came from SCS Software's own
wiki alone (modding.scssoft.com/wiki/Documentation/Tools/Dedicated_Server — "these files are necessary
for a dedicated server to start") **without checking whether the chosen Docker image papers over that
requirement.** It does: `LsHallo/ets2-dedicated-convoy-server`'s `Dockerfile` (fetched raw, not
summarized) `COPY`s a baked-in `default_packages/<ets2|ats>/server_packages.{sii,dat}` pair into the
image at build time, and `entrypoint.sh` runs `cp -n /default_packages/... "$SAVEGAME_LOCATION"`
(no-clobber) on every container start. **The server boots and hosts a fully working vanilla base-map
convoy with zero customer file, immediately, on first order.**

A customer who owns paid DLC maps or wants mods active still needs their own exported
`server_packages.sii`/`.dat` (SCS's own wiki: "these files are NOT linked to your account in any way" —
there is no way to fabricate a valid one for a specific customer's DLC/mod ownership) — but getting it
onto the server needs **nothing new**. This platform's existing root SFTP/file-manager access
(`lib/sftp.ts`, `lib/actions-files.ts`, `components/customer/files/FileBrowser.tsx`, already reachable
from the customer dashboard's Files tab) reaches the exact host directory (`/opt/ets2` / `/opt/ats`,
bind-mounted by `prisma/seed-wave11-games.ts`'s setupScript) the container reads those files from —
identical shape to how ark/rust/satisfactory/mordhau/tf2/plutonium already tell customers to add their
own maps/mods/saves over the same file manager (confirmed by reading their marketing-page copy — this
is an established, live platform pattern, not something invented for this wave). No new upload feature,
no new job type, no new Prisma model. `lib/game-mods.ts`'s `ets2`/`ats` `MOD_INFO` entries carry the
customer-facing instructions (export via the game's own console command, then SFTP both files into
place and restart) — worth noting honestly: `MOD_INFO` itself is not currently rendered anywhere in the
live UI (confirmed by grepping every `.tsx` for the import — zero hits, platform-wide, for every
family, not just these two), so today the ONLY place a customer sees this is the marketing page's FAQ
(the same channel the ark/rust/satisfactory precedent already relies on) — a real, pre-existing,
platform-wide discoverability gap worth a future fix, not something this wave introduced or needed to
solve.

**Shipped:** `lib/games.ts`/`lib/game-config.ts`/`lib/game-control.ts` entries for both families, real
Steam CDN key art (`public/games/art/ets2_*.jpg` / `ats_*.jpg`, sourced from each title's own CLIENT
app id — 227300 ETS2, 270880 ATS, NOT the dedicated-server tool's app ids 1948160/2239530 — nominative
product-ID use), `app/(marketing)/euro-truck-simulator-2-server-hosting/page.tsx` and
`.../american-truck-simulator-server-hosting/page.tsx`, `lshallo/ets2-convoy-server` +
`lshallo/ats-convoy-server` Docker images (79 stars, 50k+ pulls, actively maintained), 3 GamePlan tiers
each (1GB $2.99, 2GB $4.99 popular, 4GB $7.99 — all capped at 8 players, SCS's own real ceiling, tiers
differ only in RAM headroom for DLC/mods). Every schema field carries an explicit `envKey` mapping the
game's own `server_config.sii` field name (`lobby_name`, `max_players`, `server_logon_token`, …) to the
Docker image's literal `-e ETS_SERVER_*`/`-e ATS_SERVER_*` name, same discipline as Valheim's
`world`/`WORLD_NAME`. No `worker/index.ts` changes were needed — unlike Palworld/Rust/CS2/Arma
Reforger, this game has no RCON/admin-console protocol at all and no secret to mint at provision time.

**Verified this session:** `applyGameConfigEnv` (the real function, `worker/game-variant.ts`) run
directly against both real setupScripts with 11 distinctive test-marker values per family (22 total) —
every `envKey` substituted correctly, and a negative control confirmed the original default values were
genuinely replaced, not left in place by a no-op regex. TypeScript typecheck: 0 errors (every

obtain on its own without explicit human sign-off (this repo's own `CLAUDE.md`: `/opt/nxeon` is LIVE
PRODUCTION). What was checked instead, by reading the real code rather than guessing: `lib/ipam.ts`'s

content.text:
## Summary

**Task complete.** Branch `feature/ets2-ats-truck-sim` in worktree `/opt/nxeon-staging-ets2ats` (off current `main`, commit `d2f4a99255`), not pushed, not deployed.

### The upload-requirement finding (the important part)

I re-investigated the exact blocker the prior wave (`prisma/seed-wave10-games.ts`) cited for declining ETS2/ATS — "the dedicated server cannot start with real content until the customer uploads a `server_packages.sii/.dat` pair... a file-upload flow this platform doesn't have." That conclusion came only from SCS Software's own wiki ("these files are necessary for a dedicated server to start"), without checking whether the candidate Docker image papers over it.

It does. I fetched `LsHallo/ets2-dedicated-convoy-server`'s `Dockerfile` and `entrypoint.sh` directly off raw.githubusercontent.com: the image bakes a **default vanilla `server_packages.sii/.dat` pair** into `/default_packages/<ets2|ats>/` at build time, and on every container start `entrypoint.sh` runs `cp -n /default_packages/... "$SAVEGAME_LOCATION"` (no-clobber). **The dedicated server boots and hosts a working base-map convoy with zero customer file, immediately, on first order.**

A customer who owns paid DLC maps or wants mods still needs their own exported `server_packages.sii/.dat` (SCS's wiki: these files mirror the exporting client's exact DLC/mod ownership and "are NOT linked to your account in any way" — there's no way to fabricate a valid one for a specific customer). But getting it onto the server needs **nothing new**: the platform's existing root SFTP/file-manager (`lib/sftp.ts`, `lib/actions-files.ts`, `components/customer/files/FileBrowser.tsx`) already reaches the exact bind-mounted directory (`/opt/ets2`/`/opt/ats`) the container reads it from — the identical shape ARK/Rust/Satisfactory/TF2 already use for "bring your own content." No new upload feature, job type, or Prisma model was needed.

### What I implemented
- `lib/game-config.ts` — ETS2/ATS schemas, fields keyed on `server_config.sii`'s real field names with `envKey` mapped to each image's verified `ETS_SERVER_*`/`ATS_SERVER_*` vars (fixed an app-ID mixup of my own along the way — SCS's wiki explicitly warns not to confuse the game's client app ID with the server tool's)
- `lib/games.ts`, `lib/game-control.ts`, `lib/game-mods.ts` (the SFTP instructions), `lib/game-player-recommend.ts`, `lib/game-update-verify.ts`, `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts`, `components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx`
- Two marketing pages + sitemap entries, real Steam CDN key art, `prisma/seed-wave11-games.ts`, `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` Wave 11 section
- `worker/index.ts` deliberately untouched — this game has no RCON/admin secret to mint

### Verified vs. not
- **Verified**: `applyGameConfigEnv` (the real function) run against both real setupScripts with 11 distinctive marker values per family — all 22 substitutions correct. `tsc --noEmit` clean. Full suite: 1422 tests, byte-identical 40 pre-existing/environmental failures before and after (diffed against the untouched Arma/CS16 reference worktree) — zero regressions.
- **Not verified**: a real Proxmox test provision. That needs production DB/Proxmox credentials, which I judged a background session shouldn't obtain without explicit sign-off — same call the reference wave made. I instead hand-verified the port/IPAM wiring by reading `lib/ipam.ts` and `worker/index.ts`'s `provision()` in full, and designed `GAME_PORT`/`GAME_EXTRA_JOIN_PORTS` specifically to avoid the "admin-port retraction" code path so nothing gets deleted.

I also flagged one genuine, platform-wide, out-of-scope gap via `spawn_task`: `MOD_INFO` is populated for every game family but never actually rendered in any dashboard UI — today it only reaches customers through marketing-page FAQ copy.
